Blink was one hard 50/50 square wave locked to t=0: no short flash, no dimming instead of vanishing, and two blinking layers could never alternate because every instance read the same clock — duty, dims-to and phase fix all three. **I wrote the twinkle wrong first and the test caught it**, which is worth recording: the per-star phase came from a hash with no avalanche step, so on a 96px plate every star got a phase of about 0.004 and they all dimmed in lockstep — a global flicker, not a twinkle. It was invisible at the obvious sample time too, because sin(1.5) is 0.997 and the dimming rounded clean away, so the control read as completely dead rather than wrong. Fixed to use the same mixing the line above it already used.
- v9.05 — **A tab showing an older copy of a project can no longer save it over your newer work (#306).** You reported that refreshing sometimes brings back an older version of the project, and that you had said so before. Here is what I found. Two tabs on the SAME project were completely unguarded: tab A holds an old scene, you do real work in tab B, then you switch back to tab A — and tab A's hidden-tab handler immediately writes its stale scene straight over the good one. Refresh, and you get the older version. On a phone that is not an edge case at all, because backgrounding the browser fires that handler in every open tab at once. The existing protection only ever covered a different case (a second tab open on a DIFFERENT project). Worse, nothing could even detect it: a saved project carried no notion of which of two versions was newer, so the app could not tell your project from an old copy of it. Every save now stamps a version number that only goes up, and a save that would move it BACKWARDS is refused — the tab says so and stops writing until you reload, rather than silently destroying the newer file. The same change closes a second route to the same symptom: a save that fails silently (a full store, which is much easier to hit on an iPhone) used to be indistinguishable from one that worked, so the app carried on as if saved and the next reload served whatever was last written successfully. Writes are now read back and verified. **Honest limit: I could not reproduce your particular instance** — this machine's browser allows far more storage than a phone does, so I could not make a save fail here. What I did was find the mechanisms that produce exactly the symptom you describe and close them, with a test that drives the two-tab sequence and fails if the older scene ever wins. If it happens again, tell me and it is a third cause.
- v9.06 — **Glass stops looking like TV static, Fractal Warp finally moves (EFFECTS-PLAN round 20).** Glass regenerated its distortion for every individual PIXEL, which is the one setting at which it reads as television static instead of glass — real glass distorts in facets several pixels across. It has a facet size now, a rain-streak mode that displaces along one axis only, and a seed to reroll the pattern. Fractal Warp's noise field never moved at all, and organic boiling churn is the single thing a fractal warp is for; it now has a churn speed, a feature size, and an octave count so you can have a slow smooth swell instead of fine detail. Channel Remap was completely binary — the whole swap or nothing — so it could only ever be a novelty rather than something you would leave in a finished grade; it takes a mix, and a Keep-brightness option so a swap reads as a colour shift rather than also changing how light the shot is (swapping red and blue on a sky otherwise brightens it by a third). **One high-impact effect is deliberately left: Stroke.** Its request is for an inside or centred outline and a ROUND corner, and the current one is a square-by-construction box dilation — a round stroke needs a real distance transform, which is a build rather than a slider. Doing it properly is its own job rather than something bolted onto the end of this round.
- v9.07 — **Stroke can go inside, sit centred on the edge, have round corners and a soft edge (EFFECTS-PLAN round 21).** This was the last high-impact effect in the plan and the only one that was not simply a missing slider. The outline was drawn by growing the shape in a square — which is what a box dilation does — so an inside or centred stroke and a ROUND corner were not omitted, they were impossible with that method. It now measures the real distance from every pixel to the edge of the artwork, and all four controls fall out of that one thing: outside is a band beyond the edge, inside is a band within it, centred is half of each, and softness is just where the band stops. The difference is easy to state: on a circle, the old square method bulges out to 14.25px on the diagonals when you ask for 10px, while the round one holds exactly 10px the whole way round. Inside now adds nothing at all outside the shape, which is the entire point of it — text and logos keep their silhouette instead of getting fatter. Defaults are untouched and measured unchanged (22ms against 23.8 before, because it is literally the old code path), so every existing stroke renders byte-for-byte as it did. The new options cost more: 35ms for a square inside stroke, 64ms round, and 128ms for round+centred+soft, which is the one combination that has to measure both sides of the edge. **That empties the high-impact column of the effects plan** — 33 smaller ones remain.
- v9.08 — **Sharpen stops amplifying grain, Box Blur can smear one way, and Inner Blur stops drawing a dark rim (EFFECTS-PLAN round 22).** Sharpen only ever crunched a one-pixel halo at full strength everywhere, so flat sky and skin had their grain amplified exactly as hard as a real edge; it now has a radius (wide radius is local-contrast "clarity" rather than edge sharpening), a threshold that leaves flat areas alone, and a brightness-only mode so colour noise is not multiplied along with the detail. Measured: the grain in a flat half went from 3596 changed pixels to zero with the threshold on, while the real edge beside it still sharpened. Box Blur was locked to a square kernel and one pass — it can smear purely horizontally now, and repeating the pass loses the hard boxy falloff (a straight 20px ramp becomes a soft 44px S-curve). And Inner Blur had an actual bug: it averaged colour while ignoring transparency, so near the edge of any shape it mixed in the transparent BLACK outside it and left a dark rim that had nothing to do with your artwork — on a flat disc the rim dropped from 230 to 152. "Ignore outside" fixes it, and is off by default because that rim is what your existing projects currently render. Gaussian Blur is in this family on the plan but is not done: it is a CSS filter, so laying softness over a sharp image needs a compositing path rather than a slider, and that is its own job.
- v9.09 — **The four film-look grades stop being one slider each (EFFECTS-PLAN round 23).** Each of these had its character welded into a constant, so the single Amount slider dragged several unrelated things along together. Bleach Bypass tied colour loss to contrast harshness — but keeping the bleached CONTRAST while keeping the COLOUR is the entire point of the real process, and now you can: saturation holds at 0.72 against the source's 0.70 while the tonal range still stretches from 128 to 242. Teal & Orange split warm from cool permanently at mid-grey, so whether faces landed in the orange half was decided by how the shot happened to be exposed rather than by you; the split point moves now, and the crossover can be tight or gentle. Faded Film drove the milky blacks, the contrast crush, the desaturation AND a warm cast off one control, so a COOL faded look simply did not exist — the tone control crosses zero into blue now. Cross Process had its whole look in six hardcoded numbers; the colour cast and the curve are separate, and turning the cast off leaves just the gamma.
- v9.10 — **Bend, Squeeze, Inner Pinch and Tunnel can be aimed (EFFECTS-PLAN round 24).** Bend only bowed left/right with the arc always peaking at the vertical middle; it can bow up/down now and you choose where the peak lands. Squeeze's waist was likewise nailed to the middle and always pinched horizontally. Inner Pinch's disc was hardcoded at 60% of the frame, dead centre — its size and placement being the only two things that matter for a localised pinch. Tunnel's mouth was stuck at 30% of the frame and locked to the centre, so it could be neither resized nor aimed. **And this round caught a real bug in my own work, which is worth writing down.** Squeeze's original line reads `Math.PI*y/H`, which JavaScript groups as (PI × y) ÷ H — not PI × (y ÷ H). Routing the same number through the second form changed 357 of 2030 test points at the DEFAULT settings, i.e. it would have silently re-rendered every squeeze in every existing project, with nothing visible going wrong. The plan warns that comparing new code against itself passes when both sides are equally wrong; this is that warning coming true, and the suite now carries its own written-out copy of the original arithmetic so it can never happen quietly again. It took two attempts to write that check properly — the two groupings agree on about 82% of the frame, so four sampled points all landed in the agreeing majority and proved nothing.
- v9.11 — **The app now looks like itself from the very first frame (towards #306/#292).** `theme-glass.css` — 475 lines, 75 rules — only applies when the page carries `data-theme="glass"`, and that was being set by settings.js, which loads at the BOTTOM of the page after about 1.5MB of scripts. So every load painted the bare stylesheet first and only snapped to the real appearance once that script ran. The comment in settings.js spelt out the consequence itself: with the attribute absent the app falls back to the bare stylesheet, "which is exactly the Classic look". It is in the markup now, so it is in force the moment the page parses, and settings.js merely agrees. The guard reads index.html as SHIPPED, because by the time any test runs settings.js has already set the attribute and checking the live page would pass either way. **Being straight about this: I do not think it is the bug you reported.** I rendered the page with every script stripped — which is literally first paint — before and after, and the layout was already correct both times; the fix changes colours (the inspector goes from a blue-grey to the proper dark teal) rather than the shape of the app. It is a real flash and it is gone, but it is not an old-looking version of FreeMotion. My next suspect, written up in the request so it is not lost, is the service worker: it falls back to a cached copy of the page whenever a refresh's network request fails, that cache is never rotated, and a stale page would then pull in stale scripts — handing you a genuinely old build. If it happens again, look at the version chip: if it shows an OLD number, that confirms it and I can stop guessing.
- v9.12 — **The three matte cleanup tools stop needing each other (EFFECTS-PLAN round 25).** All three exist to tidy up a key, and each one forced you to stack a second effect to finish the job. Matte Choker eroded on whole pixels with a hard square kernel and no softening, so a choked matte kept stair-stepped edges — it feathers in the same pass now, with an edge-contrast control to re-harden the ramp so a feathered matte does not go milky. Matte Fringe painted an opaque flat band with hard inner and outer edges, which always read as a pasted-on sticker rather than a rim light; it has strength and softness, taking it from 2 distinct colours to 57. Smooth Edges could only shrink the matte into the artwork as you softened it, with a visibly banded straight ramp — there is a choke to push the edge back out and a smoother falloff option that widens the ramp by over half. One thing worth recording from building it: most effect kernels in this file are a single very long line, and adding an explanatory // comment in the middle of one silently comments out the rest of the function. It broke Smooth Edges the moment I did it, and I reverted and redid it with the function expanded.
- v9.13 — **Four more colour effects stop being one setting each (EFFECTS-PLAN round 26).** Solarize was a hard per-channel flip at full strength — always a 100% harsh colour break — and now softens, mixes back, and can flip on brightness instead of tearing the channels apart. Spot Colour snapped everything outside the kept hue to 100% grey and never boosted the colour it kept, so the one hard sin-city look was all it did; it drains partially now, boosts the kept hue, and can invert to grey out the chosen colour instead. Four-Colour Gradient lerped straight toward the gradient, so at any usable amount it painted over your footage — it can Screen, Multiply, Overlay or Soft-light against the picture now, which is what a colour wash actually is, plus a spread control. And Night Vision was hardcoded green with fixed grain, so amber, white-hot and blue scope looks were impossible.
- v9.14 — **Dots, Hexagon Array, Mosaic and Dissolve stop being one pattern each (EFFECTS-PLAN round 27).** Dots had its dot-to-cell ratio and its opacity both hardcoded, so the only pattern available was "medium dots at 85%" with hard aliased edges. Hexagon Array locked its line weight to 12% of the cell, so scaling the hexes always dragged the line thickness with them and a large cell with a fine line was impossible. Mosaic could only make square, averaged, gapless blocks — it does wide scanline cells, a tile grid with gaps, and crisp nearest-neighbour retro sampling now. And Dissolve was one static salt-and-pepper pattern, identical in every project, that ate the frame uniformly with hard-edged holes and never moved; it can sweep in from any side, soften its holes, and boil over time. Two of my own mistakes are worth recording because the tests caught both: the sweep was written BACKWARDS — "from the left" ate the right-hand side, and the total number of holes was identical either way, so only counting them per half of the frame showed it. And Mosaic's block geometry could not be measured at all on the standard test image, because it varies so fast that every block averages to the same colour; it needed a picture that changes smoothly in both directions.
- v9.15 — **Border Frame, Contour Lines and Contour Strips get their controls (EFFECTS-PLAN round 28) — and that is the effects plan's whole table done bar two.** The border was welded flush to the very edge of the layer with hard square corners at full opacity, so a matte-style inset frame, a rounded one, and a subtle translucent one were all unreachable; it insets, rounds and blends now. Contour Strips had its alternating strong/weak opacities hardcoded, so the recolour was all-or-nothing and always landed in the same places. And Contour Lines had a real problem rather than a missing knob: it traced its bands off RAW brightness, so any real footage shredded into confetti instead of forming contours. Smoothing the brightness BEFORE banding it is what turns noise into contours — 30% fewer stray marks on a noisy image — and it can now draw as a clean topographic map on white paper rather than only scribbling over the picture. **What is left of that plan:** Spin and Flip Layer, which work on whole canvases rather than pixels and so need different handling, and Gaussian Blur, which needs a compositing path. Five more the plan itself says to skip. Everything else in it is built.
- v9.16 — **Spin and Flip Layer get their controls — and that is the whole effects plan's table finished.** Spin started at exactly 0° at every clip's start, so two spinning layers could never be offset from each other, and it always turned about the layer's centre; it takes a start angle and a pivot now. Flip Layer flipped in place and threw the original away, so all it could ever make was "the same layer, backwards" — it can hinge the reflection out to one side and keep the original, which is how you build a symmetry composite. **Where the plan stands: 105 proposed upgrades, all built except Gaussian Blur (which needs a compositing path rather than a slider) and five the plan itself says to skip.** The only genuinely unbuilt features named anywhere in it are Corner Pin, LUT import and Curves — each needs a new kind of control (on-canvas drag handles, a file picker, a curve editor) rather than another parameter, which is why they were always last.
- v9.17 — **The AI could not switch on any tick-box or pick any source layer — it silently wrote garbage instead (BUG-HUNT backlog).** When the assistant added an effect, it ran every parameter through a clamp against that parameter's minimum and maximum — but a tick-box and a layer-picker have neither, and clamping against nothing produces NaN. So the registry's perfectly good default was thrown away exactly WHEN the AI supplied a value. It then failed silently in both directions: NaN is not null, so every downstream "use the default if missing" check sailed straight past it, and NaN saves into the project file as null. In practice: ask for Apple-style rounded corners and you got a plain rounded rectangle, and every effect that points at another layer — Displacement Map, Luma Matte, Compound Blur, Match Grade, Polar Displace — came out with no source at all and did nothing. Six parameters across the catalogue, all of them broken, none of them complaining. Fixed, plus the capability list the model reads now describes a tick-box as "0|1" rather than "undefined..undefined", which is what invited a number into a control with no numeric range in the first place. The guard is written over the WHOLE catalogue rather than one effect, because the defect belonged to the parameter TYPE.
- v9.18 — **Exporting a transparent GIF or PNG could permanently delete your project's background colour (BUG-HUNT backlog).** To render with transparency the exporter set the project's background to nothing for the duration of the export — but that is the SAME object the app saves to disk, and the app saves automatically the moment you switch to another app or lock your phone. So: tick Transparent, start a long export, put the phone down — and the save that fires writes "no background" into your project. The exporter put the colour back in memory afterwards but never re-saved, so the file on disk kept the null until some later save happened to run. If the app was force-quit first — most likely right after an export, which is the most memory-hungry thing it does — the project reopened with no background at all, and every render and export after that was missing it. The same window could also bake a background-less thumbnail into your project list. Fixed by the general rule rather than the one case: a render option is now a temporary flag the renderer reads, and never a change to saved state. Worth noting the test needed two halves — driving the flag proved the mechanism was safe, but putting the old line back still passed, because nothing here runs a real export. It now also checks the shipped exporter contains no assignment to the project background at all.
- v9.19 — **Dragging several clips at once no longer silently changes the spacing between them (BUG-HUNT backlog).** Each clip in a multi-selection was stopped independently at its own left limit, so the moment a SHORT clip could go no further it froze while the longer ones kept travelling with your finger — and letting go made that permanent, keyframes and all. The worked example: a 6-second clip at 4s and a 1-second clip at 0.5s, dragged 3 seconds left, and the gap between them quietly goes from 3.5s to 1.9s. Nothing warns you; each bar just stops on its own. The selection now works out a single limit for the whole group before it moves, so it stops as one the instant its most-constrained clip would run out of room, and everything keeps its spacing. Dragging one clip on its own is unchanged — with nothing else selected the shared limit works out to exactly the old one. The comment a thousand lines further up the same file already stated the rule this broke: a hold-move on one selected clip must not silently break the others' relative sync.
- v9.20 — **Copying a keyframe from one effect could paste it into a completely different effect (BUG-HUNT backlog).** An effect keyframe remembered its position — "the first effect's amount" — which is fine on one layer and meaningless on another. Copying onto another layer is a feature the app advertises, and dozens of effects share the parameter name "amount" with wildly different ranges: Twirl runs -360 to 360, Grayscale runs 0 to 1. So copying a Twirl keyframe of 140 and pasting it onto a layer whose first effect was Grayscale drove that 0-to-1 control to 140 — fully desaturated from the paste point onward — and saved it. Worse, if the target effect had no parameter of that name at all, the paste INVENTED one and wrote the junk into the project file, while you saw no keyframe appear and got no error. The clipboard now remembers which kind of effect the keyframe came from and refuses to paste into a different one, and it will never create a parameter an effect does not have. Pasting between two layers that DO share the effect still works exactly as before — that is the point of the feature, and the test checks it, because a fix that simply refused every cross-layer paste would have passed everything else.
- v9.21 — **"Template saved" could be a lie, and the space it took was never coming back (BUG-HUNT backlog).** Saving a template writes the heavy part — the layers plus full copies of every video and image in the project — into the big storage area, then writes a small index entry into the small one. If that second write failed because storage was full, the app said "Template saved" anyway: the code returned success without ever checking. So the template never appeared in your list and could not be recovered, while its copy of all your media sat in storage with nothing pointing at it — and the boot-time cleanup was written to skip exactly that kind of key, so the space was gone for good. The same shape of mistake was in Save as element, Save selection as element, and Import font. All four now check, roll the heavy part back, and tell you the truth; the cleanup also collects packs nothing references instead of skipping them blind. One thing worth admitting: I spent a diagnosis cycle convinced normal saving was broken, because I had been calling it with its two arguments the wrong way round — it takes the NAME first, then the project. The A/B against the previous version is what showed me it failed there too, i.e. that it was my test and not the app.
- v9.22 — **The eye that hides a layer is finally big enough to tap (BUG-HUNT backlog).** It was a 15x15 pixel icon — about 4mm, against the 44px that counts as a touch target — sitting inside the track head, which selects the layer when you tap it. So missing the eye by 8px did not miss harmlessly: it selected the layer and slid the inspector sheet up over the timeline instead of toggling visibility. The icon has not moved or changed size; only the invisible area that responds to a finger has, and the thumbnail beside it still selects as before. Every other small control in the stylesheet had already been given this exact treatment — the trim handles, the keyframe dots, the favourite stars — the eye was simply the one that got missed. **Also struck a second finding as STALE rather than fixed:** the report that the floating + button covered the row-reorder handles at the bottom of the screen. Re-measured in exactly the state it describes, that button no longer renders at all — the Add-layer row replaced it — so its proposed fix would have reserved empty space for a control that is not there.
- v9.23 — **Keyframes on trim-path, the repeater, the dash offset, mask paths and audio effects can finally be copied (BUG-HUNT backlog).** The timeline drew a diamond for all of them, but copy kept its own shorter list of which properties it knew about — so Copy on those diamonds returned nothing at all, and because it returned nothing the "Paste keyframe at playhead" item never even appeared. Your copy silently vanished. Delete had the same gap and had been patched by hand at some point; copy never was, which is exactly what keeping two hand-written lists guarantees over time. There is now ONE list that delete, copy and paste all read, and a test that fails the moment they could drift again: every property that draws a diamond must be addressable, so adding a new animated thing to the app and forgetting the list is caught immediately rather than in six months by a user whose copy did nothing.
- v9.24 — **The X and Y boxes in Move & Transform go dead the moment they touch a snap line (BUG-HUNT backlog).** Drag the X number and the instant it reached the middle of the frame — or either edge, or any X the layer sits at on one of its own keyframes — it stopped, and no amount of further dragging moved it. Measured on the phone: X walked 600 → 552, snapped to 540, then sat on 540 for the remaining ~190px of the drag. The box re-read the value before every step and the snap had already rewritten it, so each 1-6px of movement was rubbed out before the next event arrived; only a single jump bigger than the 8-unit snap radius escaped. A scrub gesture now remembers where it started and how far it has travelled — which is exactly what the Move trackpad beside it always did, and why only the number boxes were stuck — so a snap grabs on the way in and releases on the way out. It is one shared `scrubGesture` used by BOTH number scrubbers, so a third cannot be added later without it. Two faults the bug report had not spotted, fixed by the same change: the identical read-back made Motion Blur **Samples** completely immovable (0.08 per pixel into a whole-number round is always the number it started from) and killed **Crop Width** on any project narrower than ~1400. Dragging far past a hard limit no longer banks travel you have to un-drag before the value moves again. Verified live at 375px, before and after, with the snap itself confirmed still working; two mutation checks.
- v9.25 — **Undo inside the mask editor was being silently thrown away the moment you touched a point (BUG-HUNT backlog).** Editing a mask path, pressing undo, then dragging any point put the whole pre-undo shape straight back and committed it — the step back was gone, and nothing said so. Before that even happened the teal overlay stopped agreeing with the picture: it kept drawing the old shape while the layer itself snapped back, so the handles sat visibly off the mask. The editor took one copy of the point list when it opened and worked from that copy forever; undo replaces every layer with a fresh object parsed from the snapshot, so the mask the editor was aimed at became a different object holding different coordinates while the copy stayed behind. It never noticed, because it finds its layer and its mask by id and both ids survive. Now it follows the model: it re-points itself whenever the mask it was seeded from is no longer the one the scene holds — checked by the undo itself the instant it swaps the scene (a drag starting before the next animation frame would otherwise still be too early) and again every frame by the overlay's own draw loop, which covers loading a project. **A second bug fell out of writing the test:** the double-tap-to-delete timer outlived the editor, so closing and reopening it within a third of a second and tapping the point that happened to share an index with the last one you touched deleted that point. Checked the other on-canvas tools while in there — point-edit re-reads the live layer on every operation, and crop, fill-drag and text-edit hold no geometry, so this was the only one. Verified live at 375px with the overlay photographed back on the restored mask; two mutation checks, one per test.
- v9.26 — **A group was being drawn at full project resolution and then thrown away down to the preview's size — 16x the pixels, every frame, on the project he measured (queue 125 (partial), queue 202 (partial), queue 95 (partial)).** Every other buffer in the compositor is allocated on the TARGET's pixel grid: effect plates, the camera plate, the manual-blend plate. Exactly two were not — the plate a group is flattened onto, and the plate a mask blend mode rasterises through. Both were built at project size and never stamped with the render scale, so the drawing code inside them ran at 1:1 no matter how small the preview actually was. On the phone report in that entry — a **3024x4032 project, 12.2 megapixels**, inherited from an imported photo, previewing into a 762k-pixel canvas — that is **16.0x the pixels needed**, allocated, cleared and drawn per group per frame. An ordinary 1080x1920 comp on a phone previews at about 0.48, so it was **4.3x** there, measured live. Export is untouched by construction: an export canvas is exactly project-sized, so the scale is 1 and every number is what it always was, and there is a test asserting that. **This is asserted as a SIZE, not a timing** — that entry records four passes that measured this area on a fast Mac, found acceptable milliseconds and moved on, and a pixel count is the same number on his phone as it is here. A third test compares a quarter-scale render against a full-scale one pixel by pixel, because a saving that changes the picture is not a saving. **Being straight about what this is not:** the scene in his own measurement had no group in it, so this is a real cost removed, not proof his lag is fixed. The 12.2-megapixel project itself is still the biggest thing in that report and still needs answering.
- v9.27 — **Importing a phone photo into an empty project was creating a 12.2-megapixel composition — that is where his slow project came from (queue 125 (partial), queue 202 (partial), queue 95 (partial)).** The first file you import sets the project's size, and it took the file's pixel dimensions verbatim with no limit at all. A stock iPhone still is 3024x4032, so dropping one into an empty project built a **12.2 MP** comp — bigger than anything the app's own Canvas settings picker offers, whose top entry is 2160p. That is exactly the project in his own measurement: 8 layers, 2 effects, 4 cores, half-second frame stalls. It is capped now at the short side the picker's largest preset means — 3024x4032 becomes 2160x2880 — with the aspect ratio kept, both sides even (H.264 refuses an odd dimension, so an uncapped import could produce a project that would not export), and a message saying it happened and where to change it. Nothing at or under the top preset is touched, which is tested for four common sizes. **Anyone who genuinely wants bigger can still type it into Canvas settings** — this governs only the size the app picks unasked. **Second fix, same shape as v9.26:** the onion-skin ghost plate was project-sized AND reassigned every frame, and assigning width/height reallocates the whole backing store — a 48 MB allocation thrown away twice per frame on his project. It is on the preview's pixel grid now and only reallocated when the size really changes; measured live at 380px, 518x921 instead of 1080x1920 on an ordinary comp, with the ghosts photographed still landing in the right places either side. **What this does not do:** it cannot shrink a project he has already made — Canvas settings does not rescale existing layer geometry, which is its own job — so this stops it happening again rather than repairing his current file.
- v9.28 — **Changing a project's size no longer scatters everything in it — which is also what lets an oversized project finally be repaired (queue 125 (partial), queue 202 (partial), queue 95 (partial)).** Canvas settings has always let you change the width and height, and it has always done only that: every layer kept the pixel coordinates it had, so resizing a finished composition threw the work wherever those old numbers happened to land, silently. That is a bug on its own, and it is also why v9.27's import cap could not rescue the 12.2-megapixel project it was written for — shrinking it would have wrecked the layout. There is a **Scale the layers to fit** switch under Size now, on by default, shown only when there is actually something to move. **The list of things that have to move is short, and short for a reason:** nearly everything lives inside a layer's own transform and follows its scale for free — a shape's width, a font size, a stroke, a repeater's offsets. Only three kinds of value are in absolute project pixels: a ROOT layer's position and scale (root only — a child's numbers are already parent-local, and scaling both ends applies the factor twice, which is a mutation check of its own), pen-mask paths (canvas-space points with no layer transform at all), and drop-shadow blur and offset (`shadowBlur` is device pixels by specification and the current transform does not touch it). Pixel-measured effect parameters move too, read from the registry's own `unit: 'px'` rather than a hand-written list, and clamped back into each slider's declared range. A different aspect ratio uses the smaller factor and re-centres, so the work stays whole instead of stretching. Undo puts back the size AND the geometry, verified. **The main test renders both sizes and compares where the pixels land** rather than checking arithmetic — and the cheap count assertion deliberately runs after the render, because first it short-circuited every mutation and left the picture untested.
- v9.29 — **THE TIMELINE WAS DRAWING EVERY CLIP 18px LEFT OF THE TIME IT WAS AT, in every project, since v8.55 (queue 327).** His words: *"the timeline is actually broken and is starting early"*, *"every project is broken the same way"*, *"refreshing page didn't fix"* — and it could not be fixed by refreshing, because nothing was wrong with the saved file. The playhead is a fixed line at the middle of the screen with the timeline scrolled underneath it, so the entire geometry rests on one number: how wide the track-head column is. That number was read with `getComputedStyle(document.body)` — and since v8.55 the narrow head has been declared as `#tl-tracks.tl-no-groups { --head-w: 72px }`. A custom property cascades DOWN, never up, so body went on reporting the 90px default while the column rendered at 72. **A project without a group — which is nearly every project — therefore drew t=0 eighteen pixels away from the line that means t=0.** Measured at 375px: clip at x=169.5, playhead line at x=187.5. It now MEASURES the column that actually rendered instead of reading a constant off some other element and hoping the two agree, so a future rule can move that variable anywhere and the geometry cannot come apart from the layout again. The test asserts the thing the geometry exists for — a clip at t=0 lands on the playhead line — in both the group and no-group layouts, and checks the two layouts really do differ so neither case can quietly stop covering the other. The whole suite was green throughout the ten months this was broken, because nothing had ever asserted it. **Also in this release: the Presets card shows each preset rendered ON YOUR LAYER** (the unnumbered "Check I changed the right Presets" item, which his answer today finally settled — he meant the inspector's Presets card, and wanted it to work the way the effects browser already does). Every row is a live tile of this layer with that preset applied. The tile is produced by running the REAL apply on a throwaway clone, not by a second description of what applying does — a preview that could disagree with the button beside it would be worse than no preview, and that seam is now a test. A preset this build cannot apply gets no tile, because there is nothing it could honestly show.
- v9.30 — **Auto-tracking froze the whole app for its entire run, and could then tell you it worked when it had not (BUG-HUNT backlog, two findings that had to be fixed together).** Press Track and everything after the decode ran as one uninterrupted block — both match passes, the template adaptation, the simplification and the keyframe write — so the browser could not draw until the whole thing returned. The app locked solid, nothing scrolled, and the "Tracking… 40%" toast the code goes to the trouble of computing was written to the page and never once appeared on screen. On a phone a multi-second block like that also risks the OS killing the tab. It stands aside every eighth frame now. **The yield is a MessageChannel post, not requestAnimationFrame:** rAF stops firing in a hidden tab, so switching apps mid-track would park the tracker forever, and a 0ms timer is floored to a second or more when backgrounded — the exporter learned both the hard way and its note says so. **And that fix makes the second bug easier to hit, which is why both are here.** A live editor means the clip can be undone or deleted while the track runs, and the tracker was holding the layer object it started with: after an undo that object is detached from the scene, so the keyframes went into an orphan, were silently discarded, and it still reported "Tracked — 47 keyframes added". You were told a minute of work had succeeded and found nothing on the clip and nothing to undo. It re-checks the layer is still the one in the scene. **A mutation check earned its keep here:** deleting the write-site guard survived the whole suite, because on a long clip the walk bails first and the write is never reached — the assertion was dead. It is only the last defence on a SHORT clip, which is now its own test.
- v9.31 — **Dragging a song that drives an audio-reactive layer recomputed the whole track's loudness sixty times a second, and kept every copy (BUG-HUNT backlog, two findings, one root cause).** Computing one of those envelopes is a pass over the clip's ENTIRE decoded audio — roughly eight million float operations on a three-minute track — and the key it is cached under folds in the source clip's start, trim, duration and speed as well as the behaviour's gain, attack and release. Every one of those moves continuously under a gesture: dragging the song rewrites its start on each pointermove, and the Smoothing slider derives attack and release from its position. The accessor runs per layer per frame. So the drag itself stuttered to unusability on a phone, and each pass permanently retained a ~100 KB array pair in a cache with no cap and no eviction anywhere in the file — a ten-second drag stranded tens of megabytes that nothing ever freed, ending in a mobile-Safari reload. Now: the cache is a bounded LRU, and **a signature must be seen twice before anything is computed**. During a gesture every frame produces a key that is never seen again, so nothing is computed at all; the moment you stop, one compute runs. Counting sightings rather than comparing with the previous key is deliberate — two behaviours on different layers reading the same song alternate keys every frame, and a previous-value check would have starved both forever, which is its own assertion. Export is untouched: it prewarms explicitly before its frame loop. The second finding was filed as *unverified* and it was not — same cause, and the test measures it: 40 settled looks used to leave 40 envelopes resident.
- v9.32 — **Cancel during "Decoding frames…" was a dead button (BUG-HUNT backlog).** The decode is up to 900 sequential seek-and-capture operations, and it had no cancellation hook of any kind — the exporter only checked its cancel flag BETWEEN layers. So pressing Cancel while the overlay read "Decoding frames… 12%" set a flag that nothing read: the app went on seeking and decoding for the whole of that clip (tens of seconds at 1080p, minutes at 4K, since each frame waits up to half a second), allocating up to 1.5GB of bitmaps you had just said you did not want, and only then noticed. On a phone that is both an app that feels dead and a real out-of-memory risk. The decode takes an abort signal now and reads it every frame; the frames already made are freed and NO cache is stored, because a half-length cache is worse than none — the compositor would play the clip from it as though it were complete. The export also stops immediately afterwards instead of carrying on into the audio mix, the AAC probe and the muxer before its next check. **The signal is opt-in**, so every other caller of that decode — the preview, the tracker, the reverse cache — is untouched, and that is one of the three assertions. **A second finding in the same area was struck as STALE rather than fixed:** the report that MP4 export crawls when the tab is backgrounded had already been fixed under queue 47 (partial), and the code carries the measurement in a comment. Re-checked by reading the live code rather than trusting the entry.
- v9.33 — **Benchmarks and the whole ruler sat 18px right of the playhead — the other half of v9.29's bug, which I had only half fixed (queue 334).** His report: *"when I add benchmarks they don't add where my playhead is"*, with a screenshot of the yellow pin clearly right of the white line at 00:00:00. He was reading it exactly right, and it is the same defect as the one fixed two releases ago, seen from the other side. v9.29 fixed the JS — the code that READS the track-head width was reading it off the wrong element. It did not fix the CSS, which DECLARES the narrow head as `#tl-tracks.tl-no-groups`. The ruler row is a **sibling** of `#tl-tracks`, not a child, and a custom property only cascades downwards — so the lanes rendered a 72px head column and the ruler reserved 90, and every tick and every benchmark pin was shifted by the difference. Measured live at 375px before the fix: clip at t=0 on the playhead line at x=187.5, the tick for t=0 at x=205.5. The declaration now sits on the element that contains both halves, so they cannot disagree by construction. **The test is the real fix here.** v9.29's version asserted the CLIP and nothing else, and that gap is exactly what let the bug survive its own repair — it now checks everything that stands for a time (the clip, the ruler tick, a benchmark's centre, and that the two halves reserve the same head width), in both the group and no-group layouts. A finding like this should not need him to find it twice.
- v9.34 — **Two ways the easing-curve button quietly edited the wrong thing (BUG-HUNT backlog), fixed together because each made the other worse.** (1) In Rotate mode the editor knew about the flat spin and NOT about the two 3D tilt channels, while the panel beside it keyframes all three — so picking a preset eased the spin and left the tilt linear. Measured: after Ease In-Out, at a quarter of the way through, rotation was 11.25° (eased) and rotationX was 37.5° (still linear, should have been 33.75°), so the two halves of one rotation drift apart for the whole segment, in preview and in export, with nothing on screen saying half of it was skipped. The editor's list of channels is now held equal to the panel's BY A TEST rather than by both being written out correctly — they are separate tables in separate files and that is what let them disagree. (2) The editor edits every channel of a mode together, and for a channel whose animation had already ENDED it fell back to that channel's last segment — so a preset picked at the playhead silently re-shaped a move that finished a second earlier, invisibly, because the graph only ever draws the first channel. Measured: x keyed at 0/1/2s and y at 0/0.5s, playhead at 1.5s, pick Bounce, and y's long-finished 0→0.5s move became Bounce too. Ended channels are dropped now — unless every channel has ended, where "the last one" is the only sensible reading and the single-property editor has always relied on it. **These interact:** widening Rotate to three channels means more chances one of them finished early, so fixing the first alone would have made the second easier to hit.

  Also, from checking rather than remembering: **six OPEN items were sitting below the "## Done" heading in REQUESTS.md** — including "exported video came out with no audio" and the entry that file calls the most serious thing open. The tooling always found them (it scans the whole file), which is exactly why nothing caught it; but that file is written for Ezra to read, and under a Done heading they read as finished. Moved back, and `tools/next.sh` now refuses to print a quiet list when it happens — checked both that it fires and that it does not cry wolf.
- v9.35 — **A reversed or slow-motion clip could bake the WRONG PICTURES into itself, permanently, if you touched the timeline while it was preparing (BUG-HUNT backlog — the highest-impact finding left).** Building that cache steps the clip's own video element and captures whatever frame it is sitting on. The preview writes to that same element from three places, every single animation frame. Nothing connected the two — so scrubbing, or just leaving playback running, while "Preparing frames…" was up meant the cache filled with the frames the PLAYHEAD was on instead of the ones it asked for. The clip then plays back showing the wrong pictures for the rest of the session, with nothing to say so. **Measured by removing the fix again: 28 of 30 frames came from the playhead.** The preview now stands down for the second or two a build takes — pausing and muting the element exactly as the builder itself does, so nothing is left audible — and picks up again the moment it finishes. Both flags it reads are cleared in `finally` blocks, so a build that throws cannot leave a clip permanently unable to seek, and that is one of the assertions. The test measures the thing that actually matters — which frame ended up in the cache — rather than whether a guard was called. **Found by an adversarial re-sweep of the whole BUG-HUNT file** (every remaining finding read against the live code by one agent, then handed to a second whose only job was to refute the verdict): 0 stale, 6 confirmed, 1 disputed. That sweep also **re-opened a finding that had been wrongly closed** — "Sample clip is dead on Safari/iOS" was marked NOT REPRODUCIBLE after being tested in Chrome headless, the one browser where a Safari-only bug cannot fire, and Ezra's own device is Safari on iOS. Also in this release: his four car photos, recovered from the session transcript rather than asking him to send them again, cropped to match the existing preview art.
- v9.36 — **"Sample clip" has never worked on his phone, and every tap of it was quietly breaking the app's audio (BUG-HUNT — the finding that had been closed by mistake).** The button picks a video container by asking the browser what it supports: it tested two webm types and then, if both failed, used a THIRD it had never tested. Safari records mp4 and no webm at all, so all three were unsupported and asking for one threw. That threw *after* the audio tone had been started, with no cleanup path anywhere — so each tap stranded a live AudioContext with a running oscillator, and **iOS allows about four before playback, waveforms, audio effects and export mixing all stop working until the page is reloaded**. It failed silently on top of that, because the function is asynchronous and both places that call it ignore the result. Now every candidate is genuinely probed, mp4 is among them, nothing supported means "let the browser choose" rather than naming a type it just refused, the file is named after what actually came out, everything it opened is closed however it exits, and a failure says so. **This entry had been marked NOT REPRODUCIBLE — a verdict reached in Chrome headless, the one browser where a Safari-only bug cannot fire.** The suite also runs in Chrome, so testing the real recorder here would repeat that exact mistake; the container chooser is a pure function taking the support test instead, so this machine can be asked what it would pick on a browser it is not. The audio-leak half has its own test, because that is the half that breaks everything else.
- v9.37 — **Pressing Play inside a clip's overhang restarted its sound from the beginning (BUG-HUNT — the one finding the sweep left DISPUTED).** A clip can outlive the file behind it: a speed ramp, a trim, or simply a layer longer than its media leaves a stretch where the timeline still has clip but the source has run out. Calling play() on an element that has already ended does not sit still — it rewinds and plays from the top. The per-frame sync had refused to resume past that point for a long time; **FM.play() never did**, so pressing Play inside the overhang restarted the audio, and the tick could not undo it because by then the element was playing rather than paused. One rule, written down in one place and simply missing from the other — the same shape as the timeline-origin bug that had to be fixed twice this week — so it now lives in a single function that both paths read, rather than being spelled out at each call site. **This is the finding the two-agent sweep could not agree on:** the auditor read the guard and called the entry closed; the skeptic went looking for a second path and found it. Being unable to refute a verdict is what makes it worth trusting, and here the refutation was right. Two of my own fixture mistakes are worth recording with it: the test first measured t=0 because FM.play() rewinds at the end of the project and the suite's default project is shorter than the playhead I set — it failed against a working guard — and the source length has to be the LONGER of the decoded and declared durations, because containers routinely undersell the file.
- v9.38 — **The crop easing button did nothing, then threw you out of the crop editor a moment later (BUG-HUNT backlog).** Open Edit Shape on a video or image you have never cropped and tap the easing-curve button: nothing happens. Tap the keyframe diamond next and the panel you were working in vanishes into an easing graph you never asked for. The two are the same bug. The panel deliberately does not stamp a crop onto a layer just to display one, and the easing sub-view is gated on that crop existing — but the button set its flag regardless and nothing ever cleared it. So the first tap armed something invisible, and the next refresh that happened once a crop DID exist (which the diamond creates) redeemed it. Dragging Width or Height did the same, for the same reason. Two changes, and the mutation checks showed they do different jobs: the flag is now dropped before the panel is even chosen, so it cannot survive a refresh whatever route set it — and the button dims and says "Keyframe the crop first" instead of being silently dead. **Removing the button's guard SURVIVED the first version of the test**, because the structural clear already covered the flag; what the guard uniquely provides is the explanation, so that is what the test asserts now. A guard whose only assertion is covered by a different guard is an untested guard.
- v9.39 — **Tapping "Remove vocals" twice built two instrumentals playing on top of each other (BUG-HUNT backlog).** The job decodes the whole file, renders it offline and loads the result before it creates the twin that marks it done — and nothing said it was already running. So a second tap re-asked the same question of a scene that still had no twin, agreed, and did the whole thing again: two identical instrumentals phase-locked at roughly double amplitude, clipping on loud material, plus a stray hidden layer in the timeline and two ~46MB files and two video elements held at once, which is an out-of-memory risk on a phone. **The second tap was the reasonable thing to do**, and that half matters as much as the guard: the only feedback used to arrive AFTER the decode, and it auto-hid after two seconds while the render carried on — so for the first several seconds of a long track the button did nothing observable at all. The message now goes up before the work starts and stays until it finishes, a second tap says it is still going instead of starting a duplicate, and the button itself goes dead for the duration. Both halves are separately mutation-checked: removing the guard decodes the file twice, and moving the message back after the decode fails on its own assertion. The flag is cleared in a `finally`, so a decode that throws cannot leave the feature switched off for the session — that is asserted too. Filed as *unverified*; it was not.
- v9.40 — **An animation saved as a preset stopped dead at its last keyframe instead of looping (BUG-HUNT backlog).** Saving an effect as a preset rebuilt each animated parameter as just its list of keyframes — dropping the sibling field that tells the renderer to keep repeating past the end. So a looping animation came back frozen on its final value. Measured: a parameter keyed 0→1s and set to cycle reads 25 half way through its second lap; the preset made from it read 50, the clamped last value. This is not an exotic setting — setting a CLIP to loop writes that field onto every animated property it has, effect parameters included, so anyone who has used loop at all had it. **The correct pattern already existed in this codebase:** the project sanitiser whitelists exactly the same two values, and the preset sanitiser simply had not followed it — the same shape as several other things found this week, where one rule is written down twice and only one copy is right. Carried through on a whitelist rather than copied, because that function's whole job is that nothing arbitrary out of storage reaches the renderer, and an unknown value is asserted to be dropped. The test goes through the real round trip (capture → save → read back → apply) and asserts what the instance EVALUATES to, not merely that a field survived. **A mistake of my own went with it:** the first version of that test guessed the storage key, so its cleanup wrote to a store nothing reads and it would have left two junk presets in his actual app — a cleanup that quietly cleans the wrong thing is worse than none.
- v9.41 — **Every "Replace media…" pinned the file it replaced, for the life of the page (BUG-HUNT backlog — the last one).** The media store's `set()` was a bare assignment, and all the teardown lived in `remove()`, which Replace never calls. So the outgoing record kept its blob URL valid and its `<video>` still pointing at it — which keeps the ENTIRE source file resident — plus any decoded audio, roughly 46MB per stereo minute. Nothing ever freed it: not deleting the layer, not switching projects, not closing it. Audition four takes for one slot on a phone and that is hundreds of megabytes of unreleasable memory, which is the kind of thing that kills mobile Safari mid-edit. Anything the store displaces is now released, and `remove()` goes through the same path rather than doing half the job — revoking the URL alone is not enough, because an element still pointing at a blob keeps its decode buffers, which is the lesson the v8.44 media work already recorded. **A record still reachable under another id is left completely alone.** Every path today stores a fresh record, but that is a property of the callers rather than a guarantee, and a wrongly freed record is a clip that silently goes blank — worse than the leak it fixes. Both halves are separately mutation-checked, including that the incoming file is never the one revoked.

  **That empties the BUG-HUNT backlog of open findings.** It started this session at 21.
- v9.42 — **A camera move now smears the whole scene — the camera half of queue 31b, and the last thing that entry was waiting on.** A whip pan never blurred, and the measurement in that entry said why: layers do not render through the camera. Every layer is drawn into one plate and the camera's transform is applied to that whole plate at composite time, so a layer's own matrix never moves when the camera does — and the per-layer blur, which works by re-projecting a layer through the change in its own matrix, had nothing at all to see. Doing it per layer would also have double-counted, re-projecting by the camera delta and then applying the camera again on top. So it lives at the composite, where it is both correct and far cheaper: ONE plate blitted N times under the camera transform sampled across the shutter, whatever the layer count, instead of N passes per layer. The camera gets its own Motion Blur tab — toggle, Shutter, Samples — because it is a property of the camera rather than of a layer, which is how every real editor has it and is the answer to "why doesn't my whip pan smear". Shutter and sample conventions are the per-layer ones, deliberately, so the number means the same thing in both places. **A still camera comes out byte-identical to blur-off**, which is asserted and is what makes it safe to leave switched on; it also declines when the camera has moved less than a device pixel. Travel is measured at the frame CORNERS rather than from the pan alone, so a dolly or a spin counts too — a zoom moves no pixel at the centre and plenty at the edges. Two of my own fixture errors are recorded with it: the first test swept the camera a thousand pixels off the subject and photographed empty background, reporting no smear against no smear.
- v9.43 — **An export whose soundtrack failed used to ship a file that PROMISED audio it never had (queue 215 (partial)).** Three ways a soundtrack could be lost were made visible in earlier releases, but the third one was still producing a broken file rather than an honest one: the audio track was DECLARED when the muxer was built and ENCODED at the very end, so a failure arrived after the promise had been made and could not be withdrawn. The header advertised a track that was never fed — a file that plays silently in one player and is REFUSED outright by another, which is the worst of the three because it is the one that looks fine. The soundtrack is encoded BEFORE the muxer exists now: if it fails, the mix is dropped before any track is declared and you get an ordinary silent video with a message saying so. The cost is holding the encoded audio during the render — AAC at 160kbps is about 1.2MB a minute, freed the moment it is muxed. **A second bug fell out of building it, and it explains how the third path stayed hidden:** an encoder error arrives on the AudioEncoder's error CALLBACK on some browsers rather than as a rejection from flush() — so the encode resolved normally on a soundtrack that had already died, and nothing upstream could tell. It rethrows now. *Stated rather than papered over: the full export rig with a stubbed encoder is still not built. What is tested is the contract the reordering rests on — a sink can be a function, and an encoder error surfaces — not the end-to-end "the muxer is built with no audio track" step, which remains argued rather than measured.*

The test measures the INK against the circle, to 0.5px, because measuring the box is what lets a wrong glyph pass. **324 — the colour is back**, taken from the add FAB he was comparing it to (a caught highlight over a tinted fill) rather than invented, and the bar itself now runs the app's accent through it instead of fading to nothing, which is what made it read as a disabled strip. **326 — an empty project gets the whole timeline**: a tall panel with a 64px + in the middle and the invitation under it, so the first thing a beginner sees is where to start. It reverts to the slim row the instant a clip exists, which is asserted, because his second screenshot is that state and it must not change. - v9.54 — **The service worker no longer downgrades you silently: one dropped fetch on refresh is retried, and if it ever does serve an old build it says so and names it — queue 306 (partial).** His report, for weeks: *"an older version of our project shows up when you refresh"*, then *"The glitch that shows the old version of FreeMotion that has a more alight motion look STILL shows up when I press refresh… it's such a big issue, PLEASE"*. **Still not reproduced on this machine — and this is the one path that fits the WHOLE description rather than part of it.** A failed navigation was answered from cache; that stale index.html names old `?v=` script urls; the worker answers those cache-first. And the fallback now records that it fired and which build it handed over, which the app reads on boot and says in plain words, pointing at the version chip that fixes it. **That turns "I cannot reproduce it" into one observation from his own phone:** if the message appears, this was the cause and the guessing stops; if the glitch happens and the message never does, this path is exonerated and the search moves elsewhere. **sw.js had no test coverage at all, and the reason is recorded in the entry — two sessions could not get a worker to install under test.** So the worker is not installed here: sw.js is fetched and evaluated in a stub scope with a fake cache and a fake network, and synthetic navigations are dispatched at it.
