- v10.42 — **Lightning strikes the layer it is on, and has five more things to turn (#403).** His words: *"Lighting bolt effect could use some other variables and work, also it should only go on top of the layers it's used on and not cover the canvas by default."* **The "covers the canvas" half was worse than it sounded:** the bolts ran the full height of the plate, and the stamp ended by *adding* alpha — `d[i+3] = min(255, d[i+3] + g*255)` — so a bolt crossing empty frame CREATED opacity there. It is bounded twice now: placed inside the layer's own alpha box, and scaled by the alpha already present with none added, so it strikes the shape rather than its bounding square. **Five new controls — Thickness, Jaggedness, Branches, Flicker and Seed — with every default reproducing the previous look exactly** (three branches is the old random midpoint; flicker 8/sec was hard-coded), so nothing anyone has already made moves. **A defaults trap nearly shipped and the queue-320 test caught it on the first run:** `FM.evalProp` on an *absent* parameter returns 0, not null, so reading the new defaults through it set thickness, jaggedness, branches and flicker all to zero for every render predating these controls — 121 lit pixels instead of thousands. This file's own idiom (`p.lift == null ? 26 : …`) exists for precisely that, and the new reads follow it. **The alpha gate took four mutation rounds to prove, which is the part worth keeping:** it is invisible from the composited frame, because alpha-0 pixels come out (0,0,0,0) whatever RGB the plate holds — so painting outside the layer is wasted work rather than a visible mark, and a rectangle fixture and then a circle fixture both let the mutation survive. It is asked of the renderer directly now, with an opaque middle and transparent margins, and the mutation reports 159 pixels written where no layer alpha sits under them.
- v10.43 — **The editor is now GATED at 320 / 360 / 390 / 430, not just checked at 380 (#405).** His words: *"make sure other peoples phones will actually fit everything nicely on screen and format correctly."* Every layout check in this project has been at 380, his own phone is 440, and neither is the narrow end — an SE/mini is 375, much of Android is 360, and the narrowest still in use is 320. There is a suite test now that loops those four widths and asserts, at each: no sideways scroll on the shell, no two controls overlapping, nothing clipped or pushed outside the transport row, no wrap onto a second line, and tap targets big enough to hit. **His layout passes all four unchanged, which was his condition** — nothing was redesigned to make it fit, and at 320 all eight transport controls still sit on one line with the pill centred on the playhead. **Writing it required fixing a real bug nobody had reported:** the desktop transport is built by physically MOVING five controls into the row (help, notes, cog, export, view options) behind a one-way latch, so narrowing a desktop window past 701px left a thirteen-control row on a phone-width screen, wrapped onto two lines — and any width sweep would have read that as "overflow at 320" when it is an artefact of the resize. The build now records where each borrowed control came from, parent and next sibling both, and hands them back when the window narrows; the mutation that restores the one-way latch reports the spill at all four widths (38px of sideways scroll at 320, undo and redo running past the right edge). **The teardown deleted the version chip on its first attempt** and the suite caught it instantly — that chip is the one control the build moves by selector rather than by id, so it was never recorded and went out with the wrapper. A one-way build hides exactly that class of mistake until someone tries to undo it. *(Clause 4 is asserted at 28px rather than 34 on purpose: his own narrow-phone rules step the buttons down to 28 at ≤340 so the row fits, and asserting 34 would fail a design he approved rather than protect it.)*
- v10.44 — **Answering "what IS the difference between the two preset buttons" — and the label was the bug (#406).** His words: *"make sure you grab my attention and let me know what the difference between saving a preset with just effects and saving a layer as a preset coz I assumed presets are just effects anyways so I'm confused… and if you realise we just have two buttons for the same thing just get rid of the one isn't just saving as effects."* Read off the code, there are **three** savers, not two: an effect row's ⋯ saves **that one effect's settings**; the Effects card's button saves **the effects list and nothing else**; and the layer ⋯ saves **everything** — every effect plus fill, gradient, outline, shadow, blend mode, colour grade, corner radius, **and the transform's animation**, with x/y stored as deltas and re-based onto the target so a preset animates the layer from where it already is instead of teleporting it. So "presets are just effects" is true of two of them and false of the third, and the third is the powerful one: it is the only way to carry a movement from one layer to another. **They are not the same thing, so nothing was deleted** — his conditional instruction did not fire, and a test now proves the distinction instead of a comment claiming it: a layer preset must capture the outline, the fill and the transform, and an effects-only preset must capture none of them. **The label was what confused him.** The layer one read *"Save layer's effects as preset…"* — his own wording from queue 182, asked for when a bare "Save as preset" said nothing about what it captured. It names the owner and gets the content wrong, and the old code comment admitted it in a parenthesis. All three now say what they take: "Save this effect as preset…", "Save effects only…", "Save whole look as preset…". The queue-182 test moved with the wording rather than being deleted, and still holds both of its original requirements. **One clause stays open deliberately:** "get rid of saving presets from this menu" came with no screenshot and there are three menus it could mean — deleting the wrong one costs a capability with no other route.

He had saved a whole-look or an effects-only preset, which live in different stores and never appear there, so a message that was literally true read as obviously false. It was also still pointing at "Save as preset", a menu label v10.44 had just replaced. It now names the effect, names the exact action that would clear it, and says where the other two kinds of preset live instead. **Nothing was hidden** — suppressing a true message because it looked wrong would have been the wrong fix, and the same confusion would have surfaced somewhere else. *(The first version of the test built the sentence itself and asserted against its own copy, which proves nothing — the classic self-satisfying assertion. It opens the real list and reads the real node now, and it FINDS an effect with no presets rather than naming one, because the first candidate shipped presets and the test failed for its own reason, which reads exactly like a real failure.)*
- v10.46 — **Open a preset, edit it, press one button, and that preset now holds what you can see (#407 clause 2).** His words: *"I just want to open a preset, edit it and then it automatically updates that preset. One tap keeps exactly the round trip he asked for and cannot destroy anything without being asked; the entry says so plainly and says he can overrule it. **"What if I wanted a copy" is answered by the button that was already there:** Save look + animations… makes a new one, Update “X” overwrites the one you came from — two buttons, two meanings, both visible at once. - v10.47 — **A template can be opened, edited, and written back over itself (#408).** His words: *"And templates need to be editable as well, currently they ain't."* **Half of it already worked and that is worth saying rather than changing:** "New project from template" forks a real, fully editable project and always has. - v10.48 — **Both ends of the add-row switch now land somewhere you can see and use (#409).** His words: sending it to the top *"doesn't take you fully see the add layer the top bit is cropped off"*, and at the bottom *"there should be some space at the bottom just to push up the last layer and not have it at the dead bottom, only if you're at the bottom of the screen tho"* — plus *"if you try to drag something from the dead bottom rn it just makes you close the app on iPhone because swiping from the bottom of ur screen does that lol"*. **The top was never a scroll bug.** `moveAddMarker` has always scrolled the row into view and it worked — the row landed exactly at the top of the scrollport, and `#tl-rulerrow` is a 22px sticky header sitting over that same edge, which `scrollIntoView` knows nothing about. So the row was correctly placed and covered. `scroll-margin` is the one thing `scrollIntoView` does respect, and the mutation that removes it reports a 22px crop — the ruler's exact height. **The bottom is padding, which answers "only if you're at the bottom" for free:** padding adds scrollable length rather than a permanent gap, so mid-scroll nothing looks different and the space only exists once you have reached the end. The `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` term is what lifts the last row clear of the iOS home-indicator band — the strip that swallows a drag and closes the app. **The test asserts the top against the RULER's bottom edge rather than the scroller's**, because the scroller's top is exactly the measurement that looked correct while he was staring at a sliced row; and it asserts the bottom by scrolling to the end and requiring the last row to sit clear of it. Both halves mutation-checked. *(Clause 4 is fixed by consequence rather than tested directly — an iOS edge gesture cannot be reproduced headlessly, so what is asserted is the geometry that causes it.)*
- v10.49 — **Dragging the add row into the edge scrolls the timeline with it (#411).** His words: *"On pc trying to drag down the add layer doesn't drag the screen down with it so you have to let go and then swipe down then pick it up again which is annoying."* **Every other vertical drag in this timeline already did this** — the reorder handle and paint-select both arm an eased, time-based edge scroll — and the add-row drag, being the newest gesture, simply never got one. It now uses the same numbers as its two siblings: a 44px zone, 520px/s top speed, eased by depth² so it creeps at the boundary and only quickens as you push deeper, with `dt` clamped so a stalled frame cannot lurch. All three feel identical under the finger. **The drop boundary is recomputed on every scrolled frame, not just on pointermove** — with a still finger at the edge the rows travel underneath it, and a marker that only updated on movement would sit frozen while the list slid past, which would have read as a second bug. **The test holds the pointer STILL inside the edge zone and requires the list to move on its own**, because a test that moved the pointer would pass on the old code too — moving is precisely the workaround he was complaining about; the mutation that stops arming the loop reports 0px of scroll. *(Noted rather than left to be found: this is now the third local copy of that loop in the file. Extracting one helper is the right follow-up, but doing it here would have meant rewriting two working gestures while fixing a third.)*
- v10.50 — **"Empty group" is "New group" (#412).** His words: *"Rename empty group to new group."* Three places, not the two the entry predicted: the add-menu tile, the toast it fires when you add one, and — the interesting one — **the tile-colour table, which is keyed by LABEL**. Renaming the tile without renaming its key leaves it looking up a colour that no longer exists and silently falling back, so the tile keeps working and merely looks wrong; the comment above that table warns about precisely that, which is why the fix added a read-only seam and the test asserts the key moved with the label rather than trusting it. The default layer name was already "Group", so there was nothing to change there. *(The suite also caught my test's own NAME containing double quotes — there is a meta-test that refuses them, because a quote in a test name truncates its own failure line in ship.sh and mutate.sh. A small gate doing exactly the job it was written for.)*
- v10.51 — **The shape tiles have sixteen colours instead of eight (#413).** His words: *"Add more colour to the shapes icons, currently the colours repeat and don't have much variety and isn't very pretty."* **Measured first, as the entry asked: eight tints, cycled by index across every shape in the tab** — so the same colour returned about every one and a half rows, which is precisely what reads as a repeat. **The sixteen replacements are generated rather than picked:** even 22.5° spacing round the wheel at one saturation and lightness, then reordered by stepping seven places each time — seven is coprime with sixteen, so the walk visits every hue exactly once and never seats two neighbours near each other. Measured on the result, the closest any two adjacent entries come is **157°**, and no two anywhere in the list are within 12°. **Generating them is the fix, not a shortcut:** queue 271's complaint about the Elements tab was "three blues, two greens" in a hand-picked list, and picking sixteen by eye is how that happens again — which is also why the test asserts the SPACING rather than the count, since a count alone would happily pass a longer list of blues. **An existing test pinned Shape's opening colour**, because #210/#258 treated Shape as the reference the other tabs were told not to copy; he has now said the opposite about Shape itself, so that pin was replaced by the rule it actually stood for — the tabs must not open on the same colour as each other, still checked. *(The Shape tab itself could not be screenshotted headlessly: `openTab` and a synthetic tab click both fail to switch the rendered sheet in the fixture. The palette is verified numerically by the test and visually as swatches at tile size in tile order, which is said plainly rather than dressed up as a screenshot of the real grid.)*
- v10.52 — **Tapping a position number opens the editor on the first tap (#414).** His words: *"The buttons that show a number for the position should be able to be tapped on and customised, so you can type exactly the number you want."* **Found them all first, as the entry asked, and almost all of them already worked:** the effect slider rows are text inputs, the transform rows are number inputs, and the Move & Transform boxes have had tap-to-type since they were written. **The exception is exactly the set he named.** The X / Y / Z readouts carry an axis, and the tap handler switched that axis and RETURNED — so on the position numbers, and only those, a tap never reached the editor. One tap now does both: the axis follows the box you touched, and the editor opens. The refresh was dropped rather than moved, because it rebuilds the card and would destroy the very element the editor is about to focus — so the axis highlight is a beat stale while you type and corrects itself the moment you finish, which already refreshes. A stale highlight for the length of one edit is a much smaller thing than a control you cannot type into. **The first version of the test proved nothing, and the mutation is what said so:** it set the axis BEFORE opening the card, and the rebuild resets it — so by tap time the axis already matched, the swallowing branch was never reached, and the test passed on the broken code. So it stopped dead the moment the finger lifted. It now samples with the same smoothing and flings on release under the same "did the finger stop first" rule the horizontal one uses — more than 90ms since the last move counts as a deliberate settle and must not throw the list. **It reuses `MOM_FRICTION` rather than taking a number of its own**, which is both the literal reading of "like dragging left and right" and the lesson recorded above that constant: queue 116 found the effect sliders had been left on the old friction under a comment claiming they matched, and two values meant to feel identical drifted apart in silence for months. One constant, two axes. The glide also stops if `scrollTop` refuses to move, so reaching the top or bottom ends it instead of spinning a rAF against a clamped value. The test releases a fast upward drag and requires the list to keep moving after the pointer is gone; the mutation that flings with zero velocity reports it stopping dead at the release position.
- v10.54 — **While you drag a layer, the switch wears its colour — and pressing it throws that layer to the far end (#416).** His words: *"Genius idea, make it so when you're dragging a layer the toggle button will change colour to the colour of that layer then when you press the toggle button while dragging a layer it will jump that layer to the top or bottom."* The reorder drag now publishes which layer it is holding, the switch takes that clip's colour on its knob and track, and pressing it mid-drag moves **that layer** instead of the add row. **The "which end" question is answered by reuse, not invention:** it takes the switch's existing rule from #373 clause 7 — the end it is FURTHEST from — so the control means one thing whether it is holding the add row or a layer, and a layer near the top is thrown to the bottom. The test asserts that direction rather than merely that something moved; the mutation that flips the comparison reports the top layer landing back at index 0. **The colour comes from the timeline's own clip-colour function, which was extracted rather than copied** — that expression has four fallbacks in it, and a second copy is precisely how the switch and the clip would end up disagreeing about which layer you are holding. `FM.dragLayerId` is cleared on cleanup so the switch returns to its own colour the moment you let go, asserted in both directions. The empty-state panel keeps its own design too, the big centred + from #354. - v10.56 — **The skip arrows sit nearer the play pill than the undo/redo group (#420).** His words: *"Move the two arrow buttons that jump you through the project closer towards the centre, I feel they are too far away from the time play button and too close to the undo redo buttons"* — followed by *"do only slightly tho… maybe even skip it if you feel till just make it worse"*. **Because he authorised skipping it, it was measured at his own 440 first, and the measurement is his sentence:** the right arrow sat 10.0px from the pill and 6.6px from undo — closer to the group it does not belong to than to the control it does. - v10.58 — **The dot in the switch is centred on whole pixels now (#422).** His words: *"The dot in the switch is slightly off centred."* **He was right, and it only shows on a 3× screen — which is why "slightly" is the exact word and why a box-level check would have called him wrong.** Measured in ink at three settings: at 380 @2× the track and knob centres agree to 0.00, at 440 @2× they agree to 0.00, and at **440 @3× — his phone — the knob sat half a device pixel right of centre, with 9 device pixels of track on its left and 8 on its right.** **The cause was a half pixel, twice:** the track's content box is 13px (15 minus its two borders), so `left: 50%` is 6.5px, and `translateX(-50%)` of a 9px knob adds another half. Centring it with `left: 0; right: 0; margin-inline: auto` uses the same arithmetic a block does — (13 − 9) ÷ 2 = 2px — which is a whole number at every scale factor. After: **9 and 9**. - v10.64 — queue 386 clause 1: videos and images get the Outline toggle back, and it needed no new rendering. The entry had recorded "there is no media stroke code at all" — true of `layer.stroke`, false of the app: the `stroke` pixel effect already grows an exact distance field from a layer's ALPHA, which is how a GROUP's border has always been drawn. So the toggle is translated into that same effect for media, in `effectiveFx` — the compositor's single answer to which effects a layer renders with — which means the outline follows what you can actually SEE on a cropped or rounded clip, and never touches `layer.effects`: it stays out of the Effects list, out of the saved document, and out of copies, so the toggle remains the one place it is owned. `canBorder` now includes video and image, so the card offers the same Outline row, Position, colour and size a shape gets. Said plainly: this was never reproduced (the entry records what was measured, and that the sibling-footer theory in it does not apply to the fit panel), but the SHAPE of the fault is real — the dots are a child of `.addmenu-body`, and that body becomes a scroller whenever the fit planner cannot plan, which is the same fault v10.19 fixed for the shortcuts panel and queue 275 for the phone sheet. Sticky rather than a DOM restructure because it is exact and free: where the body scrolls the row is pinned, and where it does not — the fit panel and the phone sheet, every case anyone sees today — it is a no-op. Verified at 380px that the Shape tab's grid and its five dots are unchanged.

- v10.67 — #429, candidate fix and said plainly as one: the phone's canvas is sized `--stage-h: 40vh`, and `#app` is `auto / var(--stage-h) / 1fr`, so ANY viewport growth splits between the stage and the timeline band — measured, a 60px growth gives the stage 24 and the band 36, and everything in the band slides down mid-gesture, the add row's + included. That is the "plus button moving around when I swipe" he reported, since browser chrome collapsing (and rotations, and the keyboard) all grow the viewport. Now `40svh` — the viewport WITH chrome showing, which does not move when it hides — with the `vh` line kept as a fallback. ⚠️ NOT verifiable here: headless Chrome has no chrome, so svh/lvh/vh resolve identically and the reproduction still shows its 24px by design. Five other causes were eliminated by measurement first (the empty state, positional drift, sub-pixel landing, the gesture path from three starting points, and a bare resize event), and two earlier guesses at the rule were measured, rejected and reverted rather than shipped.
- v10.68 — #306, a path nobody had considered: the service worker's navigation fetch was a plain `fetch(req)`, which is allowed to be answered from the BROWSER's HTTP cache — and GitHub Pages serves HTML with `max-age=600`. So for ten minutes after a deploy, a refresh could return the previous index.html without touching the network, with an `ok` response that trips none of the stale-detection built for this bug. Every `?v=` in that old page then names an old asset, which the worker answers cache-first: a complete older build, silently, on a good connection. That is the one mechanism found so far that produces his exact symptom WITHOUT firing the warning designed to catch it — which is the detail that never fitted. Navigations now revalidate (`cache: 'no-cache'`); still networked, still 304-able, one round trip. Not reproducible here (it needs Pages' own headers), and labelled as a mechanism that fits rather than a proven cause.
- v10.69 — queue 430: the offline cache no longer grows forever. Versioned assets were cached permanently and nothing ever removed the old ones — `activate` only deletes caches whose NAME differs and the name is a constant — so every release's copy of every changed file stayed. On a phone that shares one storage budget with IndexedDB, where his media lives, and a browser under pressure evicts the whole origin. Now pruned after a successful navigation (not on `activate`, which only fires when sw.js itself changes). Safety came from one design change: deleting whatever index.html does not name would have evicted CSS-referenced assets like the wordmark, so it prunes BY PATH — old versions of files the live page still uses, and nothing else; parsing nothing deletes nothing. Verified by planting entries: the superseded copy went, an unrelated path stayed, the current one survived — and the offline boot check (built first, for exactly this) still reports the app coming up with the network off.
- v10.70 — THE OLDEST OPEN ITEM: *"Playhead missing when a project opens. Needs an app restart to come back."* Two earlier rounds cleared the open path — the centreline is always in the DOM and always centred (`tests/_phopen.html`) — and the cause was one step past where they stopped. Queue 354 hides the centreline while a project is EMPTY, because the big + fills the timeline and a ruler over a blank page points at nothing; that flag was computed inside `buildAddRow`. Then: tap +, add your first layer, and every creator SELECTS what it made → a selected layer on a phone triggers the solo view → the solo branch draws no Add row → `buildAddRow` never ran → the flag was never taken off. Measured at 380px (`tests/_phhead.html`): 1 layer on screen, `.tl-empty-start` still true, centreline `display: none`. It came back on the next rebuild that was not soloed (tapping off the layer) or on a reload — his restart. A flag describing "is the scene empty" cannot be computed inside a function that only runs in some of the states it describes, so it is applied from `buildTracks`, which runs on every rebuild in every branch, and `buildAddRow` reads the same helper instead of a second copy of the condition. Mutation-proved by restoring the exact old semantics: caught, by the new test alone.
- v10.71 — queue 385, the judgement he asked for, built: **leaving a project now frees its media, and coming back puts it back — no reload.** His words: *"I think it may be worth having project not stay open and close when you leave them… incase a project is broken and really laggy then it won't effect the home menu"*, with the caveat *"I do like the effect of having a project open with the glint around it but not at the cost of a shitty system"*. Measured first (`tests/_leavecost.html`): going home released NOTHING — the scene stayed fully resident, `curId` was kept, a `<video>` was still attached with its `src` intact. His diagnosis was right. The two things he wants turn out not to be in tension, which is the whole answer: the OPEN glint is a flag on a card and costs nothing, while the cost is the decoded media. So the scene document and `curId` stay — he keeps the glint — and the media goes. Verified with a REAL imported video (`tests/_leaverelease.html`): 1 record resident → 0 on the home screen → 1 again on return, with the element's `src` restored. **Four ways this could have destroyed work silently, each closed and each mutation-proved:** (1) nothing is freed that IndexedDB cannot give back — the ids are checked against the store's KEYS first, so a record with no blob behind it is left alone rather than becoming a clip that never comes back; (2) the release hangs off the END of the card's thumbnail capture, which renders the canvas — put it in `home.open()` where it obviously belongs and every project card silently re-captures itself blank (measured: thumbnail 100% non-black, so the capture still wins); (3) "Save project file…" re-opens the CURRENT project with `keepOpen`, so home never closes and `serializeScene` would have written a .fmotion.json with the scene and no media — that path hydrates first now (measured: 0 blobs → 1); (4) it stands down during an export and while a media write is in flight, and only runs while home is genuinely open, re-checked after its own awaits. One hydrate runs at a time, because two overlapping ones would free a record the compositor is drawing from. The tap on an already-open card still starts its push in the same task as the click — the hydrate is only awaited on the export path.
- v10.72 — #395 (its buildable half; MP3 stays open and is his call): **a second audio-only export format, M4A.** His words: *"I want more export options like mp3 or whatever"*. MP3 is the one format no browser will produce — measured rather than assumed (`tests/_audiocodecs.html`: MP3 unsupported by both WebCodecs `AudioEncoder` and MediaRecorder; AAC and Opus both supported) — so shipping it would mean a CDN library for a format nothing native encodes. AAC in an .m4a costs almost nothing, because every piece already exists for the video path: the same `buildAudioMix`, the same `encodeAudio`, and mp4-muxer, which takes an audio track with no video. Roughly a tenth the size of the WAV. **WAV stays first, stays the default, and is now also the fallback** — #215 is the record of what happens when an export depends on a codec: a browser refused AAC and handed him a silent file with nothing on screen to say so. So this probes before it promises, separates the three distinct failures (no encoder in this browser; the encoder rejects this mix; the encode throws part-way), names the reason, and writes the WAV instead while SAYING it did. Nothing half-written is ever saved: an encode that produces no chunks is refused rather than finalized, because a moov advertising a track that was never fed plays silently in one player and is rejected outright by another — the worst of the three, since the file looks fine. Guarded by a test that checks the file really is an MP4 (bytes 4–7 are the `ftyp` box), that an empty mix produces no file at all, and that choosing M4A actually puts the dialog on the audio path rather than merely appearing in the list; all three mutation-proved. Verified at 380px: the label fits, the picture controls hide, the button reads "Export audio".

The suite caught it. 4 is coprime with 21, 34 and 55. Measured after: **67 distinct tints across 67 cards, zero repeats**, saturation 48%–93%, lightness 50%–76%. Both halves mutation-proved — wrapping the sequence, and flattening the tones.

In every case the video is imported AS A VIDEO and the toast says why — an import that quietly does nothing is worse, and a SILENT layer is worse still because it looks exactly like the feature working. **The sharp edge is the flag.** `FM._wantAudioOnly` is stamped when the Audio tab opens the picker, and a picker can sit open for as long as the user likes — so anything time-based would either expire mid-choice or leak into the next ordinary import and silently turn a video into a sound file. It is consumed by the batch, and the test asserts that in both directions. Mutation-proved twice: a flag that is never consumed, and a refusal replaced by an empty buffer. ⚠️ WAV is uncompressed, roughly 10MB a minute in IndexedDB — recorded against #430's storage work, and `FM.exporter.encodeM4A` (v10.72) is now a real alternative if that turns out to matter.

While measuring #443 a probe reported the top of the layer list as disagreeing by one slot — the gap appeared to open before L1 while the layer landed before L0. That reading came from inferring the gap from row TRANSFORMS ("the first row pushed down"), which is unreliable near the top: the block's soft clamp can put the gap where the row it would push is already at rest, so there is nothing to see and the probe picks the next row down. It disagreed with itself between runs. The app's own resolution is now reported straight from the code that does it — `g`, the effective gap, and the id it resolved to — and **all six slots agree**: at slot 1 the app says g=1 → before L1 and the layer lands before L1, while the transform reading said L2. So the entry is closed with nothing to fix, which is the right outcome for a lead that was never confirmed. Two things are kept from it. The seam stays, **behind `FM._dragDebug`**, because it runs on every pointermove of a drag and building an object and mapping the row list per frame in the gesture path #387 is about would be exactly the wrong place to spend — unset, it costs one property read. And `tests/_adddrop.html` now takes its VERDICT from the app's numbers and prints the transform reading as information only: a probe whose own noise reads as a bug is worse than no probe.

The velocity sampler divides by dt, so dt was 0 or 1ms at random: the failing run recorded **229 px/ms for a gesture that travels 2.5**, and when dt was exactly 0 the value was not finite — so `startScrollMomentum` returned at its own `isFinite` guard AFTER `_lastScrollFling` had already been recorded. That is exactly the reported symptom, on a machine that was not busy. The moves are spaced with real awaits now, and the test asserts the sampled velocity is a plausible one before it asserts movement, so a future occurrence names the fixture rather than looking like a product bug. **This is the same trap queue 351 recorded in this file** — "synthetic pointer events dispatched in one tick all carry the same timeStamp" — arriving by the other door: not forgetting to space them, but believing they had been spaced. Confirmed with three consecutive full-suite runs, all green. ⚠️ Why this mattered more than one red line: the ship gate is what stands between a broken build and `main`, and a test that fails at random teaches everyone to re-run it — which is exactly how a REAL failure gets waved through.

Every valid combination held**, which is a real clearance for the ramped path that once collapsed the whole timeline. **What did not hold was a malformed speed prop.** `FM.speedAt`'s own doc-comment says every call site needing a number must come through it — and its non-animated branch was `return sp || 1`, which hands back whatever truthy thing is on the layer, including an OBJECT. A well-formed animated prop is caught by `isAnimated`; a malformed one (`{keys:[…]}` instead of `{kf:[…]}`) is truthy, fails that check and escapes. The caller multiplies by it and gets **NaN source time at every sample — no picture, no error, and the same in the export.** Reachable rather than hypothetical: `.fmotion.json` is untrusted input and the load path deliberately does not re-run most sanitisers, so anything an import once let through is autosaved back and comes in unchecked forever after. `speedAt` guarantees a finite number now, and `layerLocalTime` and `layerSourceAdvance` both go through it; behaviour for every valid input is unchanged (0 and undefined still become 1, exactly as `|| 1` did). **The suite test found the second instance that the probe had missed** — the probe carried a fallback for `layerSourceAdvance` and never exercised it, while the test asserts the total window is finite before using it. - v10.90 — queue 451: **the rest of the `layer.speed || 1` sites, swept.** v10.89 made `FM.speedAt` actually return a number and routed the two functions in scene.js through it; the same raw idiom was still in the audio mixers, the caption mapper, the exporter, the inspector's re-time maths and the timeline's trim. Every one of them DIVIDES or MULTIPLIES by that value, so a malformed speed prop is a NaN buffer length — **a clip silently dropped from the export mix, or a reversed clip rendering as silence.** Eight real sites now go through `speedAt`. **What was deliberately left alone, and why:** `FM.isAnimated(x) || (x || 1) < 1` is safe — a malformed prop makes the comparison false, so the clip is treated as not-slow rather than poisoning anything downstream — and `FM.somethingAt ? FM.somethingAt(…) : raw` is a fallback for scene.js not being loaded, in which case nothing in the app works anyway. **Guarded at SOURCE level**, because most of these sit deep inside functions that need a decoded audio buffer to reach, and a test that cannot reach its subject is not a guard: the source-time test fetches the four audio/caption/export files and fails if the raw idiom returns in a path that does arithmetic on it, while allowing the two shapes above by pattern. - v10.91 — **bug hunt: trimming the head of a caption track dragged every caption out of sync with the audio.** Cue times are layer-LOCAL — `t - layer.start`, with **no trim offset** — so raising `start` slid the lot. Measured on a 1.6s track through the real trim grips: a 0.367s head trim moved a cue from **2.200–2.500 to 2.567–2.867**. Captions you had timed against the audio all move, which is the entire point of having timed them. A video head trim already compensates — it advances `trimStart` so the picture stays put while the window moves over it — and a caption track has no `trimStart`, so the offset goes onto the cues. Both now keep the CONTENT still while the window moves. **Non-destructive**: a cue pushed behind the new head keeps a negative time rather than being deleted, so dragging the head back out brings it back, the same promise trimming a video makes about its frames — asserted, including the round trip. **Three things this hunt got wrong before it got it right, all now written into the harness.** (1) The first two runs reported *"cues stayed put"* against a clip that had never been trimmed — `FM.timeline._trimming()` as a CONTROL turned that false clean into an honest "no trim ever started". (2) The reason it never started is that a TOUCH trim requires a deliberate 550ms hold before it arms (queue 336); a probe that presses and drags immediately arms nothing. (3) The probe's verdict keyed off the CLIP's start, which must change on a head trim — so it reported ❌ against a build that had just been fixed; it compares the cue project times now, which is the actual question. And the fix itself wrote the rule out twice — a mutation in the grip's copy SURVIVED, because the suite drives the seam — so there is one `shiftCues` writer with two callers, and a mutation to it now fails.
- v10.92 — **bug hunt: ungrouping threw the group's transform away, so every layer snapped back to where it was before you moved the group.** `groupSelection` is careful on the way IN — the group is created with a neutral (0,0) transform, because "any x/y here would instantly displace every member the moment they're grouped" — and `FM.ungroup` had no matching care on the way OUT: it re-parented the members and deleted the group, transform and all. Measured by RENDERING rather than by reasoning about the transform stack (`tests/_groupxform.html`): three shapes at ink box **44,89..155,199** → grouped and the group moved → **74,54..185,194** → ungrouped → **44,89..155,199**, exactly the pre-move position. Arrange a group, position it, ungroup to tweak one member, and everything jumps — a positioning decision discarded in silence. The group's transform is now composed into each member the same way `applyParentChain` composes it at render time: the parent's rotate/scale act on the child's local position, its rotation adds, its scale multiplies. Guarded with all three moved at once, so a translate-only bake fails — mutation-proved, along with dropping the bake entirely. **⚠️ An ANIMATED group transform is deliberately NOT baked and now SAYS so.** A keyframed group position cannot be folded into a child without resampling the child's own curve, and a silent approximation of someone's animation is worse than a plain sentence; the old behaviour never said anything at all. **Two false cleans on the way in, both now in the probe's header:** the ink box was measured by ALPHA, and the project draws its own background — so it read 0,0..199,199 in every state and "proved" nothing moved whatever happened; and the fixture wrote `grp.x` when a layer's position lives at `transform.x`, so the "moved" group had not moved and the row compared two identical states.
- v10.93 — **bug hunt: duplicating a group is clean, and a permanent orphan-parent sweep came out of it.** Hunted as the same family as v10.92: parenting is by ID, so duplicating a group has to re-point the COPIES of its members at the NEW group — if any still pointed at the original, the two groups would share children and moving one would move the other. Measured: 4 layers → 8, the copy has its own 3 members, and moving the copy leaves the original's members exactly where they were. **Clean.** What the hunt is worth is the sweep it produced: **no operation may leave a layer parented to something that no longer exists.** A `parent` pointing at a deleted layer breaks that layer's chain silently — `applyParentChain` walks until it cannot find the id and stops, so the layer renders as if at the root and JUMPS, with nothing said. That is corruption which surfaces three operations later as "my layer moved" and cannot be traced back. Now swept permanently over delete-a-group (which cascades into its members), ungroup, duplicate-then-delete-the-original, and undo-a-group-delete — with every step asserting the operation DID something first, because a sweep over operations that silently no-op is a green run that proves nothing. Both removal paths mutation-proved. ⚠️ One wrong expectation was corrected in the probe rather than left to mislead: it asserted the ink should DOUBLE after a duplicate, but an in-place duplicate sits exactly over the original, so identical ink is the correct result and the probe was reading it as a failure.
- v10.94 — **bug hunt: dragging a keyframe past its neighbour showed you a broken curve for the whole drag.** `FM.evalProp` is the one evaluator every animated property goes through — transforms, effect params, colours, masks, audio — and its whole structure depends on `kf` being sorted ascending by `t`: both early-outs and the pair scan assume it. **An out-of-order list does not degrade gracefully.** Swept against hostile lists (`tests/_kfhostile.html`): an unsorted three-keyframe list returns the LAST value at every time, *including at the other keyframes' own times* — the animation is simply frozen on the wrong number. The keyframe drag writes `kf.t` on every pointermove and only re-sorted **on release** (`dedupDraggedKfs`), so for the entire duration of a drag that carried a keyframe past its neighbour, the preview was evaluating that broken curve. You were choosing where to put a keyframe by watching a picture that was wrong — the same class as queue 443's lying drop-gap, in a different gesture. The sort is split out as `FM.sortKeyframes` and called per move; a handful of keyframes costs nothing. **The test leads with a CONTROL that the unsorted state really is broken**, because otherwise "sorted is correct" would pass on a build where order never mattered and the guard would be empty. Mutation-proved. The sweep also recorded, without acting on them, two garbage-in cases that are import-sanitised but not load-sanitised: a NaN keyframe VALUE propagates NaN, and a NaN keyframe TIME makes the curve jump to its last value.
- v10.95 — **bug hunt: a remote image URL in a project survived every reopen, and the compositor fetches it.** `.fmotion.json` import runs six sanitisers; the ordinary project load ran **one**. The load path says so itself — *"anything an import once let through has been autosaved back into localStorage and comes in unchecked here forever after"* — and the sharpest thing in that gap is a security check rather than a tidiness one: js/compositor.js does `rec.img.src = layer.fillImage`, so an arbitrary URL there is fetched by the browser the moment the project is drawn. **A zero-click beacon or LAN probe out of an app whose whole promise is that nothing leaves the device.** Measured through the app's own project APIs (`tests/_fillurl.html`): a shape whose `fillImage` was `https://example.invalid/beacon.png` came back from a save-and-reopen **intact**, and `fillGradient.angle` came back as the STRING `"99999"` with `type` `"url(http://evil)"` — both interpolated raw into a CSS gradient string. The value-level checks are split out as `sanitizeUnsafeValues` and now run on every load as well as every import — split rather than copied, so the two paths cannot drift into different ideas of what is safe. The heavy structural sanitisers (audioFx, masks, behaviours) stay import-only: rewriting those across his existing projects is the much larger change the load path already declines, and it stays logged rather than smuggled in. The test asserts a legitimate `data:image/…` fill still survives — a "fix" that stripped real fills would pass a naive check and quietly delete his work — and covers `javascript:`, protocol-relative and `data:text/html` variants. Both the check and the load path's CALL to it are mutation-proved: a correct sanitiser nobody calls is worth nothing.
- v10.96 — **bug hunt: v10.95's deferral is safe, measured — and the thing that makes it safe is now guarded.** v10.95 put the value-level checks on the load path and deliberately left `sanitizeTrimRepeater` import-only, on the grounds that rewriting the heavier sanitisers across existing projects is a much larger change. This checked whether that deferral hides anything as bad as the fillImage beacon. Its own comment is the lead: *"a NaN/Infinity would throw and kill the frame, and copies feeds a render loop (uncapped = DoS)"*. Measured end to end (`tests/_loadnan.html`): a project saved with `repeater.copies = 100000`, NaN offsets and string rotations comes back from a reopen with those values **intact** — and the frame renders in **0.7ms**, because the compositor clamps to `Math.min(50, c)` ("cap for perf/safety") and falls back on `isFinite` for every field. So it is not a bug: the maths would indeed die, and the DRAW PATH is what stops it. That makes the clamp load-bearing, so it is now asserted — nothing on the load path will clean a corrupted document, and removing the cap turns it into an unopenable project. **The assertion had to be rewritten to be worth anything.** A timing limit could not see it: with the cap removed, 5000 copies of a small rect still drew inside 400ms, so the test passed against the broken code, and tightening the number would only have asked a question about the machine — exactly the mistake that made the vertical-glide test flaky (queue 450). The invariant is asserted on the source instead, and mutation-proved. The probe's own render check was corrected too: it counted alpha, which is the whole canvas because the project paints its own background — the same trap as the group hunt.
- v10.97 — **bug hunt: the two branches of `exportRange()` did not agree about clamping.** That function decides what actually lands in the exported file, and the asymmetry is the smell: 'this clip' clamps to `[0, P.duration]` with `Math.max`/`Math.min` AND refuses an empty span, while 'the loop region' returned `{ from: P.loopIn, to: P.loopOut }` **raw**. `autoFitDuration` does tidy a stale region — measured (`tests/_looprange.html`), a `loopOut` of 999 on a 4s project comes back from a save-and-reopen as 4, because load's `refreshAll` runs it — but it only ever looks UPWARD (`loopOut > end`). A **negative** `loopIn` reached `exportRange` untouched: measured `{from: -5, to: 3}`, which would start the render before the project does. Both branches clamp now, and a nonsense span falls through to the whole project rather than exporting backwards. **Honest about reach:** the UI cannot write a negative region — `markRegionIn` stores `FM.time`, which is never negative — so this is document-level hardening like the load sanitisers, not something reachable by hand today. The value is the symmetry: two branches of one function disagreeing about whether to clamp is how the next branch gets written wrong. The test asserts a legitimate 1–3 region comes back untouched (a clamp that ate valid ranges would pass everything else) and mutation-proves BOTH branches, including the one that was already right — a refactor that made them symmetric by loosening the correct half would otherwise sail through.
- v10.98 — **bug hunt: fuzzed the whole document instead of hunting an eighth instance — and it corrected my own generalisation.** Seven hunts in, four of the five real finds had one shape: a value a saved project can carry that no load-time check removes. The structured containers are the opposite: `layer.effects` as a string, a number or an object throws `.some is not a function`, and one containing `null` throws on `.type` — but **none of it is reachable**, because `sanitizeEffects` runs on load and deletes a non-array outright while filtering every hostile entry to an empty array (asked directly, nine shapes, all neutralised). So this is a clean clearance, and my earlier summary that the app is "trusting at the document layer" was too broad — `effects` is covered; the gaps found earlier were specific fields the sanitiser does not reach. Guarded in the place the protection actually lives: the renderer is asserted against scalars, the SANITISER against containers. Adding container checks to hot draw code for a state that cannot occur would be cost without benefit. Both halves mutation-proved. **And the ship gate flaked a second time on the way**, with a plausible velocity (1.772) where queue 450's first cause produced a nonsensical 229 — so that fix held and this was a second cause: the vertical-glide test polled for 1.5s of WALL TIME while the glide advances on `requestAnimationFrame`, which asks a question about the machine, and a new 250-render test had just run. It counts FRAMES now, and says so explicitly when a tab is throttled to a standstill rather than reporting a dead glide. Three consecutive full-suite runs green.
- v10.99 — **bug hunt: the undo stack's handling of deleted media — CLEAN, and already well guarded.** The history stack decides when a deleted clip's media may be freed, and the code calls getting it wrong *"the worst kind of data loss"*: `deleteLayer` deliberately KEEPS the record, because undo restores JSON only, so freeing it there made an undone delete come back **blank**. Measured end to end: delete → undo brings the clip back **with its file**; redo → 130 further commits push the delete off the stack → the record **is** freed. Both halves correct, and they pull in opposite directions so a build cannot pass by doing nothing. **No bug found**, and the mutations showed why: freeing on delete is caught by four separate tests, and ignoring undo-stack reachability by two. This area was already properly defended — the new test adds the one thing none of them did, which is walking the whole user-visible sequence in a single run rather than each piece in isolation. Recorded as a clearance rather than dressed up as a find. ⚠️ Also worth noting from the mutation runs: `tools/mutate.sh` reported *"caught, but not by the test you expected"* on one attempt, which is exactly the check that stops a mutation being credited to the wrong assertion — the reachability rule is guarded by existing tests, not by the new one, because the new one's first half never discards a snapshot and so never runs that sweep.
- v11.00 — **bug hunt: the audio fade maths had no test at all, and a corrupted fade value could throw in Web Audio.** Checked coverage before picking this time — 28 audio tests in the suite and **none** touched `FM.fadeWindows` or `FM.fadeMul`, which shape the gain of every clip in the preview mix AND in the export. The code states an invariant nobody was checking: overlapping fades are scaled "so they meet at a single peak (a triangle) instead of overlapping — which would otherwise produce out-of-order Web Audio automation (a pop)". Swept over fadeIn × fadeOut × clipDur including hostile values: **342 of 726 combinations produced a non-finite window.** `Math.max(0, layer.fadeIn || 0)` gives NaN for a string or object and Infinity for Infinity, and the scaling cannot fix either — it is skipped when `clipDur <= 0`, and `Infinity * 0` is NaN. NaN is mostly harmless, because every consumer tests `fi > 0` and NaN fails it, so the fade is silently LOST rather than wrong. **Infinity is not:** `js/audio-play.js` does `linearRampToValueAtTime(vol, base + fi / pr)` behind that same `fi > 0` test, and Infinity passes it — Web Audio throws on a non-finite time, which kills playback. Coerced at the source, like `FM.speedAt`, rather than guarded at each of the three callers, because the next caller will not know. All 726 combinations now hold five invariants: finite, non-negative, non-overlapping, gain in [0,1], and a single peak. **One assertion had to be relaxed because it was wrong, not the code:** requiring a fade-out to end at silence when `clipDur` is 0 went red against correct behaviour — there are no samples to fade, and `fadeMul`'s `clipDur &&` guard deliberately skips the division. That is the queue-427 trap, caught before it shipped. Both the coercion and the overlap-scaling rule are mutation-proved.
- v11.01 — bug hunt #12, picked by COVERAGE rather than by guessing: a sweep over `js/*.js` found 232 exported `FM.*` functions and 76 never once mentioned in tests.js. `FM.moveLayers` was the highest-stakes of them — it is the one thing that reorders his layers, it is driven by TWO different UIs (the ≡ drag and the switch-throw), and a fault there rearranges his work silently. Swept every non-empty subset of a 6-layer stack against every drop target: **441 combinations, all correct**, against six invariants (nothing lost or duplicated, the moved block contiguous, its internal order kept, the untouched layers' order kept, landing immediately before the requested target, hostile input leaving the stack intact). A clean clearance — and now a pinned one, 186 of those combinations promoted into the suite. The single input that threw was `moveLayers(null, …)`, which no caller passes; guarded anyway, one line, and the log says plainly that it was not reachable rather than dressing it up as a fix.
- v11.02 — **splitting a clip made it fade to black and to silence at the cut.** A real bug, found by continuing the coverage-driven hunt: `FM.splitLayer` was one of the 76 exported functions the suite never mentioned. Fades are measured from each clip's OWN start and end, and the split handed BOTH halves BOTH fades — so a clip with a fade-in and a fade-out dipped all the way to nothing right at the cut and came straight back. Measured at a **full 1.0 deviation** at the split point, and it hit the picture, the sound AND the exported file, so a render carried it too. The head half keeps the fade-in, the tail half keeps the fade-out, and the two now reproduce the original curve exactly. Guarded by a test that samples the whole timeline before and after the cut — mutation-checked in both directions, because a "fix" that simply cleared every fade would have passed a seam-only check while quietly deleting his fades.
- v11.03 — **and the same bug again in text, louder.** A text layer's in/out animation is timed off the clip's own edges exactly the way the fades are, so splitting an animated title made it animate OUT into the cut and back IN from it. Measured on real pixels this time: the title **disappeared completely for 1.2 seconds** across the split. Both halves fixed together — the head half keeps the intro, the tail half keeps the outro. Two details that would have made a careless fix wrong, and are worth knowing: `durIn` cannot just be deleted, because it defaults to 0.6 seconds when it is absent; and zeroing it is not enough on its own, because with no duration the letters still pop in one at a time off `stagger`. Guarded by a pixel test, mutation-checked in both directions.
- v11.04 — **the biggest one of the three: splitting a clip restarted its effects.** Every time-driven effect — Drift, Spin, Orbit, Wiggle, Shake — runs on "seconds since this clip began", so the tail half of a cut got a brand-new clock and the picture jumped. Measured on real pixels: **Drift moved 211 px on a 320 px-wide canvas**, Shake 162, Orbit 160, Wiggle 46. The clock now lives in one function (`FM.fxLocalTime`) that all three call sites go through, and a split hands the tail half the phase it should have had. Deliberately stored WITHOUT a leading underscore: the obvious fix reuses `_clipStart`, which already exists — but the save/undo path strips every key starting with `_`, so that version would have worked right up until the first save or undo and then quietly reverted, which is worse than the bug. **The test almost lied.** Its first run reported a clean 0.00 for all seven effects — because the probe built the effect record by hand in the wrong shape, so no effect ever ran, and a still picture cannot jump at a cut. The test now builds effects through the app's own creation path and FAILS if the effect did not move the picture on its own, and that control has been mutation-checked too.
- v11.05 — **splitting an animated clip stranded everything parented to it.** A child kept following the FIRST half — which has just had its keyframes cut off at the split and so stops moving — while the second half carried on across the screen in plain sight. Measured: the child froze at the cut and was **80 px out of place** by the end of a 10-second clip, with nothing said and only undo to get it back. The two halves now share a lineage and a child follows whichever half actually covers the moment being drawn. Built so it costs nothing to projects that have never split a parent — a single property check decides it, before any searching — because this runs for every parented layer on every frame and slow playback is already on your list.
- v11.06 — **"Extend the start of the clip to the playhead" dragged every caption a second early.** Head-trimming a clip already knew to hold the captions still; the Extend button made the very same three edits and had simply lost that rule, so every cue on the track slid with the edge — one press, one second out of sync, silently. Both now share one rule instead of each keeping a copy, and it is driven off the movement that actually landed, so a clamped or rejected edit cannot shift anything. The test is deliberately written over EVERY way of moving a clip edge rather than the one that was broken, because the fault was a NEW caller losing the rule — so the next one that forgets it fails too.
- v11.07 — **ungrouping threw away everything the group was wearing.** An earlier fix taught ungroup to carry the group's POSITION onto its layers; it turns out that was only half of it. A group faded to 35% snapped its layers back to full brightness, and ungrouping a HIDDEN group put everything inside it straight back on screen. Both now come with the layers — opacity multiplies onto each one, hidden is inherited. Effects, a blend mode and an animated fade genuinely cannot be carried (an effect on a group runs once over the whole group; running it again on each layer is a different picture, not the same one), so instead of vanishing quietly they now say so on the way out. Measured by rendering, with an ordinary group as the control so a change to the picture means something.
- v11.08 — **grouping a group with another layer silently re-stacked your composition.** Only the rows you actually selected were pulled together under the new group — a group's own contents were left sitting where they were in the stack while its row moved, and the stack IS what draws in front of what. Measured: group two shapes, then group that group with a layer sitting behind them, and the layer behind came to the front — from an edit that is supposed to be pure housekeeping. A group now takes everything inside it along. The test reads an actual PIXEL rather than the layer list, because the first version of the check sampled the exact corner of the shapes, read empty background at every stage, and cheerfully reported that nothing had changed.
- v11.09 — a lead that turned out to be wrong, checked properly and then pinned. It was reported that duplicating a group could hand you a copy stacked differently inside than the original. Measured both ways — an ordinary group and a deliberately scrambled one of the kind older saved projects can still carry — and it does not: the copy comes out in the right order every time. Kept as a permanent check rather than thrown away, because a duplicate lands exactly on top of its original, so any difference in the copy's internal order shows up instantly as the wrong colour where two shapes overlap. That makes it a sharp, cheap guard on something nothing else was watching.
- v11.10 — **splitting a music clip silently killed every Audio Drive behavior for the rest of the timeline.** Anything reacting to that audio — a logo pulsing to the beat, a shape driven by the bass — stopped dead at the cut and sat frozen at its resting value for the whole second half, while the music kept playing. No error, nothing on screen to explain it, and it saved in that state. This was the one lead two separate passes found independently, and measuring it against a real audio file confirmed it exactly: driving on all 19 samples before the cut, dead on all 9 after. A behavior now reads from whichever half of the clip is actually playing, through the same mechanism that fixed parenting in v11.05. Worth knowing: the depth it drives at changed by only 0.3% across the join, so the join is genuinely seamless and not merely alive.
- v11.11 — **a Bounce stopped ringing at a cut.** Splitting a clip mid-bounce silenced the rest of the ring, because the seam keyframe the split inserts looks to the bounce like "nothing happened before this". The smallest of today's finds — 8.9 px, on the tail of an already-fading ring — but it is the same promise as the rest: a cut should change nothing you can see. The ring now carries across the seam. Costs nothing at all on a clip that has never been split.
- v11.12 — **moving a group clip left everything inside it behind.** The group's bar slid along the timeline while the layers in it stayed exactly where they were, so the group's window no longer contained its own contents and the picture did not move at all. The other "move to playhead" path already knew a group carries its members; this one had lost that half of the rule — the same kind of near-miss as the caption bug two releases ago, where two places do the same job and only one of them is complete.
- v11.13 — **dragging the edge of a speed-ramped clip moved the footage that was already on screen.** Trimming or extending an edge worked out how much video to eat using the speed at that one edge, which is only right when the speed is constant — on a ramp it is wrong everywhere else. Head-trimming a ramped clip by a second slid the surviving picture about four frames; extending the tail of a reversed ramped clip slid the whole thing by a full second, because the limit on how far it could grow was worked out at 1× no matter what the ramp actually did. All three paths now measure the ramp properly, and the growth limit is solved against the real curve. A flat-speed clip is the control and was correct before and after — this only ever affected ramps.
- v11.14 — a corrupted or hand-edited project file could put a **broken clip length** into the timeline. The function that works out how long a clip can be for the video behind it was the last one still doing unguarded arithmetic on the speed setting — so a speed value that is not a number (which a project file the app did not write can easily contain) came out as "not a number" and went straight into the clip's length, where it spreads through the whole timeline layout. Swept twelve different speed values: four of them broke it, and none do now. The two that have a correct answer are checked against it, so the test cannot pass by returning any old number.
- v11.15 — **a cut in a music clip dipped the sound to silence for a moment during playback.** There is a 45-millisecond fade on every clip edge to stop the click you'd otherwise hear when audio starts or stops abruptly. At a split, both halves applied it to their new edges and the two fades met — a ~90ms duck to complete silence at the join, in preview only, so the exported file sounded different from what you were editing. A seam between two halves of the same clip is exempt now, because there is no click there to protect against. Deliberately narrow: pull the halves apart and the fade comes straight back, which the test checks — an exemption that stuck would have quietly removed click protection from every clip you'd ever cut.
- v11.16 — **duplicating two linked layers together gave you copies still wired to the originals.** Select a layer and the thing it follows — or a shape and the audio clip driving it, or a child and its parent — press Duplicate, and both copies still pointed at the old layers. Move the originals and the "copy" moved with them, which reads as the duplicate being broken. All four kinds of link were affected. The cause was that the rewiring rule lived in two places and the multi-layer path had neither, so it is one rule now, applied once every copy exists — which is the only moment it can work, since copying one layer at a time means the thing it points at has not been made yet.
- v11.17 — **an effect copied in one project pasted into another still pointed at a layer that only existed in the first one.** The effects that reference another layer — Luma Matte, Compound Blur, Match Grade, Polar Displacement — carry that layer's id, and the effect clipboard outlives the project you copied from. All four were affected. The reference is dropped now when the layer it names is not in the project you are pasting into, and deliberately KEPT when it is, so copying a matte around inside one project still works — the test checks both, because a fix that just cleared it always would look correct and quietly break the thing you actually use it for.
- v11.18 — **Time Warp left a hole in the picture whenever the preview resolution changed.** The effect keeps a private copy of the frozen frame, and changing preview size throws that copy away — but the effect still believed its bar had already swept across, so it drew the frozen band from nothing and the swept area went transparent. Measured at 70% of the frame missing. It now repaints the swept area at the new size instead. Preview only, but plainly visible, and it happens on something as ordinary as switching preview quality.
- v11.19 — **using a layer as a Luma Matte source quietly switched off its noise reduction.** A layer that feeds a matte gets drawn twice in the same frame, and the denoiser treated the second pass as a fresh start — so it did no denoising AND threw away the clean frame it had been keeping, which meant the next frame was worse too. Measured at 45% more frame-to-frame noise. The second pass now reuses the result of the first. Also applies to Compound Blur, Match Grade and Displacement Map, which pull a source layer the same way.
- v11.20 — **the text box no longer hides under the keyboard: it now sits at the top of the screen, under the toolbar.** You have called this the oldest thing still not done, and the reason it survived so many attempts is that it was never a measurement problem. The box was docked flush on top of the keyboard, and every measurement said it was landing there exactly right — 73 of them, across 12 different keyboard sizes. What none of them could see is that the strip directly above the keys is not ours: iOS draws its own controls there (the ˄ ˅ ✓ bar, and the row of word suggestions), those are painted over the page, and nothing in the browser reports that they exist. So the box was being placed correctly into a space that was already taken, and no amount of better measuring was ever going to fix it. It is now docked under the toolbar at the top instead, where nothing else can cover it, and the picture sits in the space between it and the keyboard. The whole class of problem goes away rather than being measured again. The two tests that guarded the old position now guard the new one, and both say plainly that moving it back re-creates the bug.
- v11.21 — **found a fourth way an export could come out silent, and made it speak.** This is the long-running "I exported and got no audio even though the video had audio" report. Three separate fixes have already closed three ways it could happen — the mixer being unable to read a clip, the browser being unable to encode AAC, and the soundtrack failing to encode at the last moment — and each of those now puts a message on screen telling you what went wrong. This is the fourth, and it is the one that slipped past all of them, because the clip involved has absolutely nothing wrong with it. If a clip sits outside the stretch of time being exported, it is skipped — which is correct — but it was skipped in complete silence. So if that happened to be the only clip with sound, you got a video with no soundtrack and not one word anywhere explaining why. Measured: a perfectly good sound layer sitting past the end of the project produces a file with no audio track at all, and an empty list of complaints. It now names the clip and says where it is versus where the export ended. Deliberately quiet when you export a chosen section on purpose and leave a clip out of it — that is you asking for it, not a mistake, and a warning that fires when nothing is wrong is a warning that stops being read. This does not yet explain YOUR export, but it removes the last place the answer could have been hiding without leaving a trace — so if it happens again there will be something to read.
- v11.22 — **leaving a project while sketching no longer leaves you stuck in the drawing tool.** Start a drawing, go back out to your projects, and the app still thought you were drawing: come back and you were in the drawing menu again, and — worse — open a *different* project and that one was in drawing mode too, with a toolbar belonging to a sketch you started somewhere else. The cause is that the drawing tool keeps its state in one place shared by the whole app rather than inside the project you are drawing in, so nothing about loading a project ever cleared it. The odd part is that the code to end a drawing session existed all along and was correct; the app simply never called it when you left. The test drives the real "open a project" path rather than calling the cleanup directly, because a cleanup only ever called by tests is exactly how this managed to stay broken while three tests were quietly exercising it.
- v11.23 — **and the other half of the same one: leaving a project while sketching left the drawing tool painted over your project list.** v11.22 cleared the sketch when a project was *opened*, which fixed coming back to it. It did nothing about going out, and going out was the uglier half — measured, the drawing canvas and its toolbar stayed on screen on top of the home screen, still belonging to the project you had just left. Your report opened with those exact words, "when you leave a project mid drawing", and shipping only the return half would have made the round trip end clean while the middle of it was plainly wrong. The cleanup now sits next to the other things that get unwound when a project closes — playback stopping, the group view exiting, the preview zoom resetting — because a sketch is one more thing that must not outlive its project. The test asserts both ends of the trip, since the first version passed while half the bug was still there.
- v11.24 — **no app change: a tool that turns "it's laggy" into a number, and a wrong answer of mine put right.** You sent a screen recording of the app being, in your words, buggy as hell. This morning I read that file the cheap way — looking at how many bytes each frame took up — and told you it showed a flawless 60 frames a second with nothing dropped. That was wrong, and wrong in a way worth naming: a video frame still costs plenty of bytes when the picture has barely changed, so I was measuring file size and calling it movement. Decoding the actual pixels says the opposite, and backs you up completely: **96% of the frames in your recording are identical to the one before, and there is a solid 1.1-second freeze near the end.** The app is stuttering badly and visibly. There is now a small tool in the repo (`tests/_framediff.swift`) that does this properly on any recording you send, using the video decoder already on the Mac — Chrome cannot even open iPhone recordings, which is part of why this went unmeasured for so long. Nothing in the app changed in this release; what changed is that the oldest performance complaint on the list finally has hard evidence instead of "cannot reproduce".
- v11.25 — **"preset" now means one thing only: the effects on a layer.** Your words: *"presets are just for effects not anything else, if it says preset remove any other function than just saving what effects the layer has."* There were two other things in the app using that word. The **canvas preset** — "Save project as preset…" in the canvas settings, and the "Your presets" row it put at the top of the New Project screen — is gone entirely, along with anything you had saved in it. Worth saying plainly: that was a feature you asked for back at #183, so this is me removing something on your instruction rather than tidying up something stray. The effects presets are untouched — that is the one kind you are keeping, and nothing about saving or applying a layer's effects has changed. Three tests that guarded the canvas presets went with the feature, so the suite is deliberately three smaller rather than accidentally. One thing left for you to decide, which is in the list rather than done: there is also a "Save whole look as preset…" on a layer, and it saves the look **and the animations**, which is more than just effects — say the word and it goes the same way.
- v11.26 — **motion blur finally smears movement that an EFFECT makes, like a shake.** Your words from 18 August: *"Motion blur should work when other effects make a layer move, currently it doesn't, like shake effects."* It never did, and the reason recorded in the list for weeks was wrong, so it is worth saying what was actually happening. Effects like Shake, Wiggle, Spin, Drift and Orbit move a layer as they draw it, and the app peels effects off one at a time while rendering. Motion blur was being applied at the very BOTTOM of that stack — by the time it ran, the shake had already been taken off, so the blur was smearing a perfectly still layer, and the shake then shoved the already-blurred result sideways. Sharp picture, every time. The blur now runs at the TOP of the stack instead, where it can still see the shake. This is the same fix, for the same reason, as the one you asked for on Squish — *"if a shake makes it move the squish doesn't do anything"* — and it was pinned at the wrong end for exactly the same reason. Two things you should know. A blurred layer that also has pixel effects on it now has those effects inside the smear rather than painted on top, which is the more truthful picture but does change how existing projects look. And a shaking layer with motion blur on now costs real work — it has to draw the layer once per slice instead of once per frame — so it is only paid when you actually have both switched on together. Measured on a shaking square: 1326 lit pixels before, and a genuine smear after, with a check that fails if the shake ever stops moving and another that fails if a still layer starts paying that cost.
- v11.27 — **you can now keyframe Distortion's Drive and Bit Crush's Bits, and they sweep smoothly instead of clicking.** These were two of the six audio sliders that had no keyframes, and the honest reason was never "we forgot" — most effects animate by nudging a number the audio engine already understands, but these two work by rebuilding a lookup table, and you cannot smoothly slide from one table to another. Swapping it is a hard jump, which is exactly why sweeping them used to click. So instead of one table, the app now builds a row of them across the whole range and fades between neighbours — fading is something the audio engine does perfectly smoothly, so the sweep is clean. Measured: a Drive keyframed 0 → 100 over four seconds now passes through exactly the sound a fixed Drive of 50 makes at the halfway point, matching to within a twentieth of a percent, and the worst sample-to-sample jump is no bigger than a static setting's. Two things worth saying. If your Drive is just a number and not animated, nothing changes at all and nothing extra is built — an early version of this quietly allocated the whole row for every project that merely HAD a Distortion, which a check now makes impossible. And the other four sliders are still not keyframable: Lo-Fi is next, while Reverb Size, Reverb Decay and Pitch Shift work a third way again and would need their own solution.
- v11.28 — **Lo-Fi's Amount can be keyframed now too, which makes three of the six.** Lo-Fi was the awkward one: its single knob does three jobs at once — it closes a high-pass, closes a low-pass, and swaps the distortion table underneath. The first two the audio engine can slide smoothly on its own; the third is the same "you cannot slide from one lookup table to another" problem that Distortion and Bit Crush had, so it uses the same row-of-tables-and-fade-between-them trick. The catch was that both halves have to move together, or the band closes while the crunch stays where it was. Measured on a signal carrying a 6 kHz partial so the closing filter is actually visible in the numbers: halfway through a 0 → 1 sweep the sound matches a fixed setting of 0.5 exactly. As with the other two, a Lo-Fi that is just a number and not animated builds nothing extra and sounds precisely as it did before. Three down, three to go — Reverb Size, Reverb Decay and Pitch Shift work differently again and need their own answer.
- v11.29 — **no visible change: the automatic preview-quality system was put on trial and cleared, with numbers.** When playback gets slow the app is supposed to quietly render the preview at fewer pixels to keep up. Your last performance readout showed it sitting at its highest quality setting while the app crawled at 10.7 frames a second, which looked exactly like a safety net that measures the fall and never opens. Driven directly for the first time, it behaves correctly on all three counts: it steps down repeatedly when that genuinely helps, it tries once and then stops when it does not (rather than softening your picture for nothing), and healthy frames never provoke it. That is now a test, and deleting the step-down turns the suite red. The measurement that matters for you is the other one: your scene — nine layers carrying twenty-four effects at that canvas size — takes **163 milliseconds a frame on a fast desktop Mac**. That is about six frames a second before your phone is even involved, so the slowness is not a fault, it is the sheer amount of work. The quality system is the right answer to it, and the reason yours read "highest quality" is that it only runs while something is actually playing or being dragged — so the reading was taken when it had never been asked. **One more readout, taken while the video is playing, settles it.**
- v11.30 — **the intro video is 77% smaller and looks the same.** It was 2.84 MB, which was more than the entire app's code, and the whole of it landed on someone's first visit — on a phone, on cellular, at exactly the moment they decide whether this app is any good. It is now 0.62 MB. Nothing about it changed that you can see: same three seconds, same sixty frames a second, same 180 frames, same look. The saving came from the fact it was stored at 2048×2048, and the screen only ever shows it at the width of its short side — about 1320 pixels on your phone — so more than half the pixels were being downloaded and then thrown away. There is a side benefit you may notice: there was a comment in the code explaining that a 2.8 MB file leaves a long window on a phone where iOS draws its own play button over the splash, and a file a quarter of the size shortens that window considerably. The black is verified unchanged, which mattered more than it sounds — the splash's black is matched to the page behind it on purpose, and lifting it would have brought back a visible seam.
