It was only ever asked when you opened a project from the Home screen, and a refresh does not do that — it restores your last document straight into the editor — so the case the warning exists for was the one case it stayed silent for. It stays quiet on Home and on a first boot with nothing restored.
- v12.09 — Saved elements no longer come out as black cards (queue 488). The picture was taken at whatever moment the playhead was on, so a selection whose clips sit elsewhere on the timeline drew nothing and the card came out solid black — indistinguishable from every other one. It now picks a moment the selection is really on screen, keeping the playhead when that already shows it, and refuses to save a black card at all: anything that can never draw falls back to the ✦ / letter card instead.
- v12.10 — The lag report's audio line now describes the ten seconds it sampled instead of the whole playback (queue 489). The counters run from the moment you press Play, and the report was dividing that running total by its own window — so the longer you had been playing before pressing Measure, the bigger the number, and past a threshold the report flatly blames FreeMotion's rate correction. A sample with 3 real rate writes in 1.2 seconds was being reported as 746 per second. The sync-error figures are still whole-session and now say so on the line itself.
- v12.11 — The "this project is too big" instructions moved inside Canvas settings (queue 490). Tapping the warning used to fire an 11-second toast and then open the dialog on top of it 400ms later, so you had 0.4s to read it and the rest of the time it was a blur behind the card. The guidance now sits in the dialog itself, for as long as you are choosing a size, and shows for anyone who opens Canvas settings on an oversize project. The card also gained a height limit so a longer note cannot push Apply out of reach.
- v12.12 — The lag report's sync-error figures now come from the ten seconds it says they do (queue 491). Collection stopped after the first 600 samples and only restarted when you pressed Play, so the numbers printed under a "10-second sample" heading were from a window that had closed long before — and drift building up over a long playback could never show. It keeps the most recent samples now, timestamped, and the report takes only its own.
- v12.13 — The "playback is struggling, tap to measure" offer now really does need 120 struggling frames in a row (queue 492). The count was only cleared by a frame that came in fine, so it survived pauses and drags — one late frame after an unrelated pause could tip a total left sitting at 119 from earlier, and since the offer only ever appears once per page load that false alarm spent it. It clears when playback stops and again when you press play.
- v12.14 — The lag report's sync-error samples keep the latency correction that v11.70 introduced (queue 493). The sample was worked out at the bottom of the sync tick, and a seek clears the learned bias a few lines above it — so after every seek the raw error, output latency included, was stored instead of the corrected one and inflated the "worst" figure. The tick that learns the bias no longer stores its own answer either: that value is zero by construction and was pulling the median down. The report's three known faults are now all fixed.
- v12.15 — Export is reachable again on a short phone (queue 494). With the silent-export warning and the custom size/fps rows showing, the card grew to 633.6px in a 553px window with nothing able to scroll — 15.2px of the Export button was visible and there was no way to reach the rest. The card now has a height limit and scrolls, and the Cancel/Export row is pinned to the bottom so the settings move behind it while the buttons stay put. The canvas dialog and the export-ready card share the same markup and get it too.
- v12.16 — The "this export will have no sound" warning now follows the format you pick (queue 495). It was worked out once when the dialog opened and never again, so choosing Audio only (WAV) left it warning you about a format that needs no codec at all — the very reason WAV is the first audio option. It applies only to MP4 and M4A now, the two that actually encode AAC, and is re-asked on every format change.
- v12.17 — The tappable toast can be used from a keyboard (queue 496). It announced itself as a button and took focus, but nothing happened when you pressed it: only a real button gets Enter and Space for free. Enter and Space now activate it, Escape dismisses it, and the countdown waits while it has focus. Also closed a leak found on the way — the audio-reactive sheet's window-wide key blocker could outlive the sheet, which would kill every keyboard shortcut in the app.
- v12.18 — Electric Edges is visible now (second round of the effects quality pass). Sweeping all 105 effects at the settings they ship with and ranking them by how far the pixels they touch actually move, the median scores 131 and Electric Edges scored 2 — five times below the next weakest. It measures edges with a Sobel filter and divided by that filter's theoretical maximum, which no real edge approaches, so it was drawing a one-pixel line about 4% of full brightness. Nothing visible was lost by fixing it, because there was nothing visible to lose. A test now fails if any effect drops under a visible floor.
- v12.19 — Canvas settings no longer hides its last row behind the buttons (queue 498, a regression from v12.15). Pinning that button row used one offset while its background used another, so the row was dragged up over whatever sat above it — and on a card that did not scroll, "Scale the layers to fit" was covered with no way to reveal it. The export dialog gains the same correction: scrolled to the end, its last setting is now fully clear of the buttons. Also: the effects sweep now covers the 21 warp effects it had been silently skipping.
- v12.20 — Holding the timeline no longer offers to clear every marker (queue 499). Rename and Remove stay, since they act on the marker you are pointing at; with both that and "Add marker here" now gone, a long press on empty ruler opens nothing at all rather than a menu with one destructive item in it.
- v12.21 — In select mode the help and delete buttons join the group on the right instead of stranding mid-bar (queue 500). One stray line was doing it: the bin carried a fixed 52px right margin that ate the space the selection label is supposed to absorb, so the label stopped short and left a 56px hole before the group buttons. The margin was reserving room for the ⋯ button, which select mode hides.
- v12.22 — The add-row switch is white at rest and flashes blue for a moment when you press it (queue 501). The blue now means something: the add row it moves is usually scrolled out of sight, so the flash is the only confirmation the press landed. It still wears the dragged layer's colour while a layer is in hand. The whole look sits behind one constant in js/app.js, so it can be undone in a single line.
- v12.23 — Dragging a layer up or down now updates the picture as you drag (queue 502). Reordering changes what is on top, but the reorder was held back until you let go, so the canvas kept showing the old stacking for the whole gesture. Measured: dragging one square above another, the centre pixel used to stay the old colour until release. The new order is applied only for drawing — the project is not touched until the drop, so cancelling leaves nothing behind and the drop is still one undo.
- v12.24 — The play button loses its filled background (queue 503). The timecode pill is the play control, and it was the only thing on that row wearing a solid slab while everything beside it is a bare icon. It is transparent now with a white outline, and while playing the outline and digits go blue with the background still clear. Together with v12.22's white switch that row reads as one set of controls; both changes sit behind a single constant so they can be undone in one line.
- v12.25 — Switching between Projects, Templates and Elements no longer blanks the screen (queue 504). Every tab tap was replaying the whole first-open sequence — each card held invisible through a stagger and then faded in, with the background glow restarting underneath — so the grid sat empty for close to a second. Measured 200ms to a painted grid before, 100ms after, on a four-card screen; a full grid goes from about 0.9s to 0.33s. Opening Home still plays its full entrance.
- v12.26 — Editing an element now edits that element (the elements half of the elements-and-templates work — the item stays open for templates). Tapping one used to create a project, and the app's own "save as element" instruction made a duplicate rather than updating the original — there was no update path at all — leaving a workspace behind every time. An element can now be updated in place, the workspace is reused rather than minted per tap, and coming Home writes the edit back and clears the workspace away. Templates still need the same treatment.
- v12.27 — Editing an element now finishes the way it should. It opens with nothing selected instead of every layer at once, leaving it puts you back on the Elements tab rather than dropping you into a project, and the element you just edited moves to the top of the list. The saving itself already worked in v12.26; these three are what made it feel unfinished.
- v12.28 — The slam easter egg works with a mouse wheel again (queue 250). One wheel notch pulls the list 41.9px against a 64px threshold, so it has to build up across notches — and the accumulated pull was being thrown away after 130ms, which is less than the gap between two clicks of an ordinary mouse. A trackpad sailed past it; a wheel never got off the ground, which is why it read as completely broken on PC. One gesture is still exactly one slam, and a single stray notch still does nothing.

- v12.29 — The two rainbow ＋ buttons are different colours at last, and both move (queue 456/507). They had been using the identical conic ramp, and the home one was not animated at all — so "different colours (both moving)" was failing on both halves. Home is cool (sky/mint/periwinkle/violet) drifting its hue over 26s; in-project is warm (gold/orange/hot-pink/violet) turning on 22s while its colour breathes on 9s, so the periods never line up and it no longer reads as one slow spin. A test of mine had demanded they be identical — queue 384's "siblings" was my inference, not his instruction — and it now guards that both are real multi-hued ramps without forcing them to match.
- v12.30 — Turbulent Displace, the last effect still costing over 150ms a frame, is 4.2x faster: 151.3 → 35.8 ms measured at his own 1080x1350. It was doing eight sine/cosine calls per pixel — 11.7 million a frame — and an earlier pass (v11.7x) could only hoist half of them out of the loop, because the other half feed the first half's result back in and tangle x with y. The whole displacement field is now built on a coarse grid once a frame and read back per pixel, with the grid spacing chosen from the effect's own Detail so a fine crawl falls back to exact. The first attempt read the grid with straight lines and was out by 9.9px at Amount 80 — the measurement caught that, not the tests — so it reads with a curve instead: worst error 0.07px across Amount 6-80 and Detail 10-300, and 21 pixels of 128,000 differ on hard-edged text, where nearest-neighbour sampling rounds either way.
- v12.31 — Text Spacing gained WORD SPACING and LINE HEIGHT, the two halves of that request that were named as "still open" months ago and then left, because they change the text layout rather than adding a slider. Word spacing pushes the gaps between words without touching the letters; line height is a multiplier, so x1 is exactly what you have now and two stacked effects compound. Both default to changing nothing, so every Text Spacing already sitting in a project renders identically. Three things had to follow it: the wrap cache is keyed on word spacing too (without it a wrapped caption kept its old line breaks and the control looked dead), curved text measures each glyph on its own so the word gaps are added back by hand there, and a missing parameter now reads as "absent" rather than zero — that last one had quietly collapsed the line height of every existing instance.
- v12.32 — Fixed the timeline drawing its rows on top of each other and then refusing to redraw at all (queue 541). Reproduced exactly: start a reorder drag with the ≡ handle and let the pointer be LOST — no pointerup, no pointercancel, which is what a browser-stolen pointer or an OS window switch looks like from inside the app. Two things then held at once and together they were fatal: the rows kept the transforms that glide them apart, measured at exactly one row height so row 2 landed on top of row 1, and the timeline refuses every rebuild while a drag is in flight, so nothing ever cleared them. The DOM froze mid-drag for the rest of the session while the real project moved on underneath it. The drag's own cleanup was always thorough — it simply never ran. So the fix is not another listener for one more way a pointer can vanish: a refused rebuild now notices when the gesture it is waiting on has gone quiet, and clears the wreckage instead. That covers every drag in the timeline rather than the one way in that was found.
- v12.33 — The Add menu's two odd tiles are drawn properly (queue 543). AI Scene was the only entry in the whole menu using an emoji, so it sat among fourteen line drawings as a filled yellow glyph — and because an emoji is drawn by the platform, it was a different picture on a phone than on a PC. It is now a four-point sparkle pair, the mark AI has settled on, with no rectangle in its silhouette so it is easy to pick out among all the box-shaped tiles around it. Sample clip's lines really were going through it: the crossbar ran from x=4 to x=20, which is exactly the box's own left and right edges, and the two ticks started on the top edge — and every icon here uses a ROUND line cap, so all three ends grew another 0.9px past the border. It was never the drawing, it was the endpoints. It is a real clapperboard now, with a tilted slate above the body, so there is no line that has to stop precisely on a border for it to look right.
- v12.34 — The Template icon is a stamp: a dashed master with a solid copy in front, which is what a template actually is — a thing you make copies from (queue 546/510/432). This is the fourth attempt at this icon and the first he has chosen, and the reason the earlier ones failed is worth keeping: queue 432 drew four alternatives and "put them to him" in words, while the drawings sat in a local file he cannot open from a phone. Asking someone to pick between five icons by description is asking them to imagine one. This time five were drawn, rendered at the real 24px they ship at and beside the four neighbouring tabs, and sent to him as a picture. The palette is untouched — the orange frame and cyan/violet accents are his from queue 267. One thing was rebuilt after the first attempt: the master had been hidden behind a copy filled with the panel colour, which is only correct on a tile that happens to be that colour; it now traces just the part the copy does not cover, so it is right against any background.
- v12.35 — Fixed the Media and Audio menus on PC (queue 542). Measured on his own window: the inspector panel is 232px tall and the Audio tab's content was 344px, and nothing held the menu to the panel — the body ran from y=203 to y=302 inside a 231px box. That panel is deliberately `overflow: visible`, because the add menu's resize handle sits just above its top edge and a scrollbar would clip it, so the spill was cut off by the app shell instead. Not scrolled past, not paged: gone. Every tile below the fold was unreachable by any gesture. The rule that made the panel `overflow: visible` carried a safety argument — that the grid solver sizes the tiles to the panel, and the body has its own scrollbar when it cannot — and both halves had quietly stopped being true: the solver returns nothing at all on a panel too short to plan with, and the body could not scroll because nothing constrained it to the panel. Both are restored, so that argument holds again. Two smaller faults came out with it: the page size was computed for four columns while the CSS lays a panel library out in five, so pages were under-filled and rows did not line up; and when the solver returns nothing, the number of rows now comes from the measured height instead of the three that were measured on a phone. The phone is deliberately untouched.
- v12.36 — A song whose file will not admit its own length no longer imports as a clip with NO length, which is the shape of the long-standing "it will not play at all" report about adding a song. When a browser reports a track's duration as Infinity, NaN or zero at import — which a VBR mp3 with a damaged header does, and a phone recording always does — the app fell back to a trick that seeks to the end and waits up to a second and a half for the file to reveal itself. When that landed nothing it gave up and recorded the length as zero, so the clip arrived with no duration at all and pressing play did nothing. "Sometimes" was exactly right: whether it worked depended on how quickly the file decoded. Audio files now ask the decoder first instead, which was already known to be both righter and about twenty times faster — measured on an earlier fixture at 26.384s in 25ms, against 13.453s in 600ms for the seek trick. Video keeps the old route, which is what it was written for, and that is tested too.
- v12.37 — The timecode digits are centred in their pill (queue 509). You said you were not sure about this one, and on a desktop you would have been wrong: measured at 1000px wide the pill shrink-wraps the numbers, one pixel of space each side, dead centre both ways. At 380px I measured that same pill 226.6px wide with the digits 71.1px left of its centre — one pixel of space on the left and 143.2 on the right — because the readout had no text alignment set at all and inherited "start", so the numbers hugged the left edge. Fixed by centring the text rather than pinning a width: the note beside this rule records that pinning a width here once pushed the desktop play control three pixels off screen centre, so the box is deliberately left exactly as it was.
- v12.38 — The inspector can now be dragged up as high on its own as it could when dragged together with the timeline (queue 512). You had this exactly right, and the numbers were stark: on an 820px-tall window, dragging the panel by itself stopped at 508px while dragging it up with the timeline reached 590px — 82 pixels apart, from the same gesture on the same panel. Two separate ceilings had been written down, one for each drag, and the panel's floor is the timeline's height applied AFTER its own ceiling — so raising the timeline first quietly carried the panel past a limit it otherwise refused to cross. The panel's ceiling now asks the timeline's own limit what it allows and never sits below it, tied to that function rather than to a copy of the number, so the two cannot drift apart again — which is how they came to be 82px apart in the first place.
- v12.39 — A raised Add menu no longer gets stuck over the canvas with no way to lower it. Drag the add menu up on PC, then tap a layer: the panel kept floating at its raised height while showing that layer's options instead of the add menu — and the drag handle only exists alongside the add menu, so there was nothing left to pull it back down. Deselecting did not clear it either. The rule was already written into the code — the menu must never be left floating over a canvas it is no longer showing — and it was enforced when the window resized or the layout changed, but not for selecting a layer, which is the one thing that actually swaps what that panel is showing. Now checked on the single path every selection change already runs through. Found by driving the drag through orderings rather than by reading it, which is what he asked for: the same two taps in the other order behaved completely differently. Also removed a height that was being written to storage on every drag and never read by anything.
- v12.40 — The Director panel no longer sits on top of the timeline on PC. Opened at 1280x820 it was a fixed rail running from just under the top bar all the way to the bottom of the window, which buried 38.7% of the timeline — the right-hand 376px of it — in the one layout where the timeline is the thing you are working in. Its own content was 711px tall and did not scroll, so the extra height was not even being used for anything. It now stops exactly where the timeline band begins, and follows that band when you drag it taller or shorter rather than assuming a fixed number.
- v12.41 — The Director panel has a background of its own now, so it stops reading as one more grey dialog: sky into violet into mint, thrown from the top-right corner. You picked it from three options drawn into the real panel and screenshotted, over the quieter one I had recommended — which is the reason for drawing them rather than describing them. The colour sits where the chrome is and fades out before the content, because this panel holds your API-key field and a lot of small print, and a wash behind small text is the one thing that would make it harder to read instead of nicer to look at. Worth recording: the first attempt used a conic gradient and drew a hard diagonal seam straight across the panel at its real width — fine in the abstract, ugly on screen, and caught only by looking at it.
- v12.42 — Two fixes to the drag handles and one to the Director panel. The panel now reaches the top of the screen: it had been sitting 50px down, holding clearance for a top bar that does not exist on PC — the Studio layout moved that bar's contents into the transport row long ago, so those 50 pixels were bare background above it. Its bottom was also checked at every band height, tall and short: it stops at the timeline and scrolls its own content rather than losing any. And neither resizer keeps resizing after its pointer disappears. If the mouse button came up somewhere the app never heard about — a right-click, switching apps, the browser taking the pointer away — the drag never ended, and every ordinary mouse move went on resizing: the inspector panel followed the cursor around the screen, 432px to 492px to 232px, dragging the timeline to its floor along the way. Both handles had the same hole. Limited to a mouse on purpose: for a mouse, moving with no button held can only mean the release was missed, whereas a finger reports itself held down and sends nothing once it lifts.
- v12.43 — You can see what you are drawing again: the second and every later freehand stroke now appears the moment you lift the pen, instead of staying invisible until you pressed Done. The first stroke of a sketch creates the layer, and that path repaints the screen; every stroke after it took a different path that updated the drawing's data and the timeline thumbnail but never asked the canvas to redraw. The overlay the live stroke is drawn on is wiped as soon as the stroke is committed, so the moment you lifted the pen the stroke disappeared from the overlay without yet having been painted anywhere else. The data was always right, which is exactly why this lasted — every check of the drawing itself passed while the screen showed nothing, so the test for it counts lit pixels on the canvas rather than looking at the stored path.
- v12.44 — The sketching screen on PC is laid out for a desktop at last. The toolbar was pinned to the bottom of the window while the canvas sat up top — measured at 1440x860, 268 pixels of empty black between the tools and the thing they act on. It now sits directly under the canvas and follows it when you zoom or resize. The gap itself had a cause worth naming: drawing already hides the timeline and the inspector, but the layout still reserved their row, so the stage was 628 pixels of an 860 pixel window and the canvas was small above a strip nothing could ever occupy. Collapsing that row gives drawing the whole window and takes the canvas from 578 to 746 pixels tall. The "Draw on the canvas — keep drawing, then Done" line is gone too, as asked; the stroke count stays, because that is something you cannot see for yourself. Also checked and found fine, so nobody hunts it again: the drawing surface was never mis-sized.
- v12.45 — You can now press an eye and drag down the column to hide a whole run of layers in one go, on phone and on PC. The first eye you press decides what the sweep does, and every row you cross is set to that same state rather than being flipped on its own — so dragging back over a row does not undo it, which is what would have made the gesture useless for hiding a block of layers. The whole sweep is a single undo step rather than one per row. One thing had to change under the hood for it to work at all: hiding a layer used to rebuild the entire timeline, which throws away the very button your finger is on, so each eye is now repainted where it stands and the rebuild happens once when you let go.
- v12.46 — The three buttons that appear when a layer is selected — parent-link, bin and the ⋯ menu — sit in an outlined container now instead of a black slab. It had been 45% black painted onto a bar that is already almost black, so it read as a hole punched in the row rather than a box holding three related buttons; it is a hairline outline over a barely-there lift, so the group sits slightly proud of the row. And the bin is calm at rest and turns red the moment you hover or press it, rather than being the loudest thing in a row of quiet icons. Both of these reverse earlier instructions — the slab was dark because it was once asked to be darker, and the bin was red by request — so both were put in front of him as pictures rendered with the real buttons before anything changed, and both are the version he picked. The red has not gone: it arrives exactly when you are about to click delete.
- v12.47 — The coloured outlines on the PC inspector cards are no longer cut off at the corners. Each card was clipping its own glow: the ring is drawn one pixel outside the card, and the card had been told to hide anything that overflows it — a rule added so a long label could not stretch the tile. The ring is also drawn at a slightly larger corner radius than the clip, so the corners were sliced square while the straight edges survived, which is why it looked like a rendering fault rather than a missing glow. The crop now lives on the label, which is what it was for: long labels still crop, and the ring is free to trace the whole card.
- v12.48 — The inspector no longer overflows when a text layer is selected. The card grid works out its row height from how much room the panel has left — band height minus the title, the quick row and the gaps — and that sum was right for every layer except text, which adds a "Text to Voice" row nothing else has. So the grid was handed more height than there was, and the bottom row ran past the panel by about the height of that row, at every size. The row is counted now: a text layer fits exactly from a slightly taller band upward, and at the very smallest band, where the cards reach the size they refuse to shrink below, the panel scrolls rather than hiding anything. The count is a named value rather than another constant buried in the sum, and the test walks every layer type — because the bug was a number going stale when the panel gained a row, not the text row itself.
- v12.49 — On PC, opening the text editor now hides the option cards behind it. The phone has done this for a long time; the desktop layout never got the same rule, so the whole grid — Colouring, Effects, Presets and the rest — stayed sitting behind the editor and stayed clickable, which is what was bugging out when you pressed one. Nine live cards, measured, with the editor open. They are gone while you type and back the moment you close it, and the timeline widens into the space rather than leaving a hole. The editor itself is a floating panel over the canvas rather than part of that column, which is why hiding the column is safe — and the test checks the editor is still on screen afterwards, because hiding it along with the cards would have been a far worse bug than the one being fixed.
- v12.50 — On PC the font list fills the space beneath it and scrolls up and down instead of sideways. Measured before: the strip was 538 pixels wide holding 987 pixels of fonts, so about 450 pixels of them were hidden off the right edge, while 244 pixels of window sat empty underneath. The eleven fonts now wrap onto three rows, the picker grows to fill what is there — leaving 12 pixels rather than 244 — and it scrolls vertically once there are more fonts than fit. Your phone is untouched, which is what you asked for: a sideways swipe is the natural gesture on a narrow screen and there is no spare height to fill, and the test asserts the phone strip stays a strip rather than only checking the desktop half.
- v12.51 — **a layer can finally be dropped BELOW the add row on PC (#521), and the reason three earlier fixes missed it was the width they were measured at.** The reorder laid every row out as one uniform slot; on PC the add row is a 7px LINE, so it was handed a 43px slot it does not draw and every row beneath it sat ~34px above where the drag believed it was. Measured at 1280px: the whole band from the line down through three quarters of the next row dropped the layer ABOVE the marker, and landing below it needed the finger two rows lower. #357/#443/#480 were all measured at 380px — the one width where the add row IS a full row and the arithmetic is correct. Rows now carry their own measured pitch (identical maths on the phone, where every pitch is equal), and the drop applies the same marker index the add switch has been previewing live since #438 — the two had been disagreeing on screen the whole time. Guarded by a test that FORCES a desktop width in both suite passes and refuses to run if the add row is not the short variant. Also fixed on the way past: a drag that ended without reordering (a cancel, or a pointer the browser steals) cleared the live order preview but never asked for a repaint, so the canvas kept showing the order you almost dropped into. And ship.sh/mutate.sh now give the runner real headroom and say "ran out of time" instead of "SUITE IS RED" with no failures listed.
- v12.52 — **the export that came out silent, measured at last (queue 215 (partial)) — and it was not the muxer.** A new harness walks the exported MP4's box tree, reads each track's real sample count, then decodes the audio back and takes its PEAK. That last step is the one no previous round took. The muxer is healthy: a normal export writes 22 audio samples peaking at 0.4038. What was wrong is that SAMPLES ARE NOT SOUND — a **muted** layer, or one at **zero volume**, passes every check in the mixer (not hidden, file decodes, window overlaps), so a buffer renders, AAC encodes it and the muxer writes a full track of which every sample is zero. Perfect file, nothing failed, nothing said. Worse, **soloing a SHAPE** silences every soundtrack in the project, because solo is project-wide and a shape has no audio to solo — nothing hidden, nothing muted, no way to guess. All three now name themselves on screen: the mixer peak-scans the rendered buffer and reports "every audio clip is muted or at zero volume", and layers killed by hidden/solo report "is hidden or muted by solo" — but only when the export ends up with NO sound at all and covers the whole project, so a clip you can see suppressed stays quiet. A healthy export still says nothing, which is what keeps it from becoming the noise that kills a diagnostic. Also fixed: the AAC probe's success branch cleared the new flag one line before anything could read it, so the screen and the flag disagreed. Both new assertions mutation-proven.
- v12.53 — **on a phone, the reorder handle disappears while a layer is selected (queue 522).** Ezra's own reasoning was the specification: selecting a clip on a phone puts the timeline in solo view — one row, the selected one — so the ≡ handle has nothing to reorder against. Measured at 380px: nothing selected → 3 rows and 3 handles; one selected → 1 row and 0 handles. The desktop is asserted UNCHANGED (3 rows, 3 handles, selected or not), because "this was only mobile" is his scoping. Not built rather than hidden with CSS: a display:none handle still carries a live pointerdown listener whose gesture code reasons about a list of other rows that is empty in solo view — the one case its own comment calls out as having nowhere to drop. Mutation-proven.
- v12.54 — **the text edit screen closes itself the moment its layer stops being selected (queue 523).** It was a lifetime bug rather than a missing button: the editor is bound to one layer and never noticed the selection move on, so deselecting left the whole surface up, still demanding the blue tick — "and it's kinda glitchy", which is what an orphaned modal always looks like. It COMMITS on the way out rather than discarding, because tapping off the editor already commits and losing what you typed would be a worse bug than the one being fixed; he asked for the screen to go away, not the text. Hooked at TWO places, and the second is the interesting one: FM.selectLayer is the named API, but every layer creator writes scene.selectedId directly and calls refreshAll(), so a fix hooked only to the obvious place passes every deselect case and still strands the editor the moment you add a layer while it is open. Both are mutation-proven, and two controls hold the test down — re-selecting the same layer and a plain refresh must both leave the editor open, or a build that tore it down on every refresh would pass and be unusable.
- v12.55 — **element drafts can be thrown away by hand, and the card says which kind it is (queue 525).** Every element edit before v12.26 left a workspace project behind; those carry no element id, so the automatic clean-up correctly leaves them alone and they sat in the Elements tab with no way out. The card gained a ⋯ with Open and keep building / Delete draft… — confirmed, and nothing is ever auto-deleted, because an orphan may hold work never saved as an element. It calls discardDraft rather than remove: remove() opens another project, or CREATES an Untitled when you delete the one you have open, which would manufacture the very stray project #505 was about; discardDraft refuses instead, and the card now says why rather than looking like a dead tap. Labels split on ofElement — a workspace editing a real element names it, everything else keeps the plain draft text. It does NOT claim to spot orphans: a brand-new draft is created identically to a pre-v12.26 one, so labelling either as an orphan would be a guess dressed as a fact. Also fixed: the card was a button that needed to contain one, which is invalid nesting browsers resolve by dropping one of the two. Mutation-proven.
- v12.56 — **the play pill's outline now sits on exactly the same lines as the buttons beside it (queue 526).** Measured first: every button in that row is a 34x34 box with an 8px radius and a border of ZERO width — an invisible box — while the pill was 24.5px tall with a VISIBLE 1px border and the same radius, so the one outline you can actually see was inset 4.8px at the top and 4.7px at the bottom from the boxes either side of it. The fix is the height, not the border: 34px, digits flex-centred. Measured after at three widths — 380, 320 (both narrow tiers) and 1280 desktop — the top and bottom edges match to 0.00px at every one, the digits stay centred both ways, and the desktop pill is 0.00px off true screen centre so v4.97's assertion is safe. Shutter 4 to 12 and samples 32 to 48, which move together on purpose — the smear is `samples` copies spread across the shutter window, so a longer window at the same count is a ghost train rather than a blur. The visible effect is carried entirely by the perpendicular spread, and its ceiling (how much room the layer has to bulge before hitting the OTHER axis's walls) falls 3.2 to 1.067 to 1 as the ball nears the floor. At 1 there is no bulge, so nothing changes. That is precisely the fade seen from outside: 236, 230, 210, 160, dead. So the two walls do interact — each closes off the room the other needs. - v12.69 — **deleting a layer leaves nothing selected (queue 556), Opacity gets its easing curve (queue 557), and Lens Flare gets colours (queue 558).** 556 had TWO doors and fixing one would have been the usual half-fix: the toolbar path and the per-layer path both clear `selectedId` now, and `selectedIds` with it, while deleting an UNSELECTED layer still leaves the selection exactly where it was. 557 puts the curve button beside Opacity's diamond, gated on the property actually being animated — an easing curve edits the transition BETWEEN keyframes, so on a static opacity it would open an empty editor, which is the “diamond that does nothing” complaint from #529 in a new place. Building it exposed a worse bug next door: `inspector.back()` clears six easing flags but its CONDITION listed five, and the opacity curve is the only sub-view gated on its flag alone rather than on a `view` — so back reset the view, refreshed, and redrew the editor it was asked to leave. Back did nothing, twice, with no way out; it is in the guard now and the test asserts both doors out. 558 gives the flare TWO colours because it draws two things, the round core and the six streaks, so the anamorphic warm-core/cold-streak look is reachable rather than a single tint over the lot; both keyframe for free because #555 landed first, and both default to the warm white it was hardcoded to, so existing flares and new ones render exactly as they always did. The load-bearing detail is that #474 asserts this kernel byte-for-byte against the original six-ray implementation, which has no colour params: splitting one multiply into two is equal in exact arithmetic and can differ in the last float bit, so the kernel keeps the original single-multiply expression whenever the two colours match, and the new test pins that branch. 961 tests green.
- v12.70 — **dragging a clip past the end of the project (queue 524).** Measured before touching it, and “breaks” turned out to be worse than the entry recorded: the clip does not freeze at the limit, it runs BACKWARDS. Traced on a 4s clip in a 4s project in 45px steps, its screen position went 584 → 560 → 516 → 472 → 428 → 404 once `start` pinned — all the way back to where it started while the finger kept travelling right, which is the opposite of the gesture rather than the absence of one. The cause is the edge auto-scroll: it kept scrolling right with nowhere left to go, and each scroll shifts the drag origin, so a pinned clip slides left at the speed of the scroll. Brake 4 refuses to scroll right while the drag is pinned at its ceiling — 0 backwards steps after, on desktop and at 380px. The project also grows WHILE the finger is down now (4 → 4.74 → 5.49 → 6.23 → 6.97 → 7.71 → 8s, ruler following) instead of jumping on release, so the timeline visibly extends under the clip; grow-only, so dragging left does not re-cut the project mid-gesture and a clip moved around inside a longer project does not touch it, and release still runs the real fit so the committed result is unchanged. It failed twice in one day: v12.69 shipped #556/#557/#558 with six lower items workable, and v12.70 jumped #474 while the gate that catches it was being written. tools/next.sh printed the right answer both times; nothing was broken except the obeying, which is precisely the shape of safeguard this project treats as no safeguard at all. So ship.sh now REFUSES a release that closes an item while a lower-numbered workable one is still open. The rule lives in `next_up` beside classify() in tools/_classify.py, because next.sh, status.sh and this gate are three readers of one rule and that file's own history says a rule in two places is the most expensive bug shape here; it carries five self-tests of its own (lowest-open wins, unnumbered entries sort first because they predate the numbering, a letter suffix sorts inside its number, a blocked lower item does not hold the queue, and a declared skip releases it) and ship.sh already refuses when any of them break. An item that can never close is exactly what rots at the bottom of the list. 962 tests green.
- v12.72 — **a layer squashed into a CORNER now actually flattens (queue 539 (partial) — clause 4 of four).** The entry's own recorded measurement was wrong and is corrected in place: it said the corner produced “zero px differ”, a complete no-op, and that reading came from a BOUNDING BOX — the wall clips the box either way, so a bbox cannot see it. Re-measured, 1,410 pixels changed and the lit area dropped 8.5%. Same blindness the entry warns about one paragraph earlier, committed again inside the correction written to cure it, which is why the new test counts pixels. What was actually wrong is that the ball compressed without ever LOOKING squashed: the visible part of this effect is the perpendicular bulge, an x-squash bulges in Y, and in a corner there is no room either way so both spread ceilings clamp to 1. The parked design decision is made — the layer flattens, because a corner holding a ball rigid is not what he is describing. Corner 125x125 → 111x111, 29% less lit area, both corners; rolling in reads as one motion, 125x172 → 125x162 → 117x158 → 111x141 → 111x111, largest step 8px of smooth compression per 10px of travel against the 14px a switch would move at once. A ball against ONE wall with room to bulge is byte-identical, asserted before anything else because changing it would re-cut every existing project. **The suite refused this three times and every refusal was right**, which is the whole reason those tests exist. (1) It broke the FIRMNESS FLOOR — the cap stopping a wall compressing a layer below 30% of its own extent — because this term compresses on top of that map and was unbounded: at inset 200 a 150px layer came out 25px wide against a 45px floor, the exact nub the cap exists to prevent. (2) The both-walls rule was a HARD SWITCH: halving each wall's budget “when both are live” flips, and this function's own comments already say a hard switch pops wherever its condition is reachable on screen — instrumented through the seam, the right wall's penetration goes 0 → 1 at s=206 and the factor flipped 1 → 0.5 in one pixel of travel, reading 5.68 against a limit of 1.5. The two walls now share one budget in proportion to their own penetration, which goes to zero smoothly instead of being switched out. (3) The engagement threshold was too wide, and that one PASSED and still had to change: at 1.5 it engaged on a case that is not a corner at all — a ball squeezed between the two SIDE walls at inset 150 — taking that sweep from a measured baseline of 0.83 to 1.45, under the limit by 3%, which is a flaky test rather than a feature. The baseline was measured with the term bypassed rather than assumed, and the threshold is 1.15 now; every sweep sits at or below its own baseline. 963 tests green.
- v12.73 — **the four transport menus pop out of their own button, with a comic tail and an opening animation each (queue 548).** Measured before building, and the entry's guess was right: this is ONE mechanism, not four. The cog already did the whole thing in CSS written only for itself, while the other three opened dead centre (500,63 and 555,249) with no animation at all. js/popfrom.js is that idea generalised; after it, every one of the four has its tail within 1px of its own button's centre, sits 8-11px clear of it, is fully on screen and opens with an animation. The notepad gets its own, per his fourth clause — it does not grow, it flips open over its top edge like turning back the cover of a pad. The cog was deliberately NOT rewritten: it takes the tail and keeps its own placement and cv-grow, because two tests pin that behaviour and re-deriving it to tidy the code would risk something he can see for nothing he can see. Desktop only, and asserted rather than assumed — at 380px all four buttons are not rendered at all, so a tail would point at nothing. THREE WRONG BUILDS FIRST, all the same mistake dressed differently: placing the card from a measurement that was not its real size. Parked at 0,0 under position:fixed a card leaves its scrim's flex flow and changes size (the export card reads 367px tall there and 403px where it lands, so it was placed 10px above the button and then rendered 36px taller, back over it). Pinning the measured width to fix that was worse — the notepad's scrim stretches its card, so natural width read 1150px and the card came out nearly full-screen. Placing by transform fixed the sizing, but re-measuring mid-animation read the box AFTER the transform, so a card at scale(.86) measured 14% small and tails landed up to 63px off; it measures through offsetWidth/offsetTop now, which transforms cannot touch. The teardown was also hooked to each close path by hand and leaked on three of four — Escape does not close three of these dialogs at all — so it is driven by the card disappearing instead, which every close path necessarily does, including ones not written yet. The suite then caught a fifth fault that would otherwise have shipped: the tail was a CHILD of the card, and a tail at top:100% counts toward the scroll height of a card with overflow-y:auto — the canvas-settings test went red with “it needs 402px and has 391px”, which is exactly the 11px triangle, and the same arrangement would have let the tail scroll away inside the card it is attached to; it is a sibling in <body> in viewport coordinates now. Finally, four rounds of readings claiming the animations were stuck and every card sat 6px out were an artefact of the browser pane rather than the code (LOOP rule 11): rAF does not fire in a tab that is not fronted, a control loop returned zero frames in 500ms, and the cog's own cv-grow — which predates this work — also reported running after 600ms. That did expose a real bug, since the retry and the teardown watcher were both rAF-driven and so would never run in a background tab; both use setTimeout now. Re-measured with a control confirming animations advance: every tail is dead centre on its button, gaps 8-11px, nothing scrolls, every animation reaches finished. 964 tests green.
- v12.74 — **the head divider is no longer cut short on the add-layer row (queue 550, clause 2 of two).** The clause had been parked as “needs him to circle it again”; measuring the rendered phone layout answered it instead, and there is exactly ONE break in that divider anywhere in the timeline. At 380px every layer row draws it 41px tall at x=66, the full row — and the add row drew it 21px tall in a 40px row at x=67, half its neighbours, a pixel out sideways, with a visible 2px gap to the row below. Two causes, and the first is a comment in this repo being wrong: `.tl-addrow-head` carries `align-self: stretch` under a comment claiming that makes the rule run the row's full height, but stretch reaches only as far as its FLEX PARENT, and that parent was sized by its own content. Stretching the inner took it to 38px. The remaining 2px is the row's own box — `.tl-addrow` has a 1px border on all four sides and a 1px margin top and bottom, both transparent and both purely for spacing — which inset the rule at each end and pushed it right; the head compensates with negative margins so the line spans the row's whole slot. After: y443..485, 42px, x=66, identical to every layer row, and the gap to the next row is 0.0px. The + has not moved and the dashed box still starts at x=66, so clause 1 is untouched. Phone only and verified rather than assumed — on desktop the add row is the --line variant whose head is `display: contents`, so it generates no box and none of this applies. What is deliberately NOT changed: a 1px gap remains at every layer-row boundary, where each row's own bottom border interrupts the rule. That is pre-existing and uniform down the whole stack; the add row was the odd one out and now matches. 965 tests green.
- v12.75 — **the wipe sliders are four times finer, with their range untouched (queue 559).** The entry's own diagnosis was wrong and measuring showed it: it assumed the useful part of the effect happened across a small part of the track with most of the travel wasted, and it does not. Sampled across the whole range, Wipe is dead linear — 1, 6, 11, 15, 21, 26, 31, 36, 41, 46, 51, 56, 61, 66, 71, 76, 81, 86, 91, 96, 100 percent of the frame — and Radial Wipe is near enough, with every notch moving the picture by about the same amount (avg 2.0%, min 1.2%, max 3.0%). There was no dead zone to narrow and no response curve worth applying. The fault was RESOLUTION, and the number that names it is TICK = 7 in js/inspector.js: the strip is pushed at 7px of drag per notch and the notch fell back to the param's step, so 7px of finger travel moved 0.02 — 2% of the picture. The app's other two 0..1 progress sliders were already at 0.01, so the two wipes were the outliers, which also answers his plural. The fix uses the mechanism already here: tickQuantum refuses to draw more than ~100-120 notches, so shrinking the step alone would have been coarsened straight back, and a row can instead force its own notch — how the Speed slider got its range in #455 — except effect params had no way to reach it. `q` now travels from the catalogue through the registry to the strip, and it had to be added to the registry's rebuild explicitly because that normaliser lists the keys it knows and drops anything else silently, which is the trap #482 recorded when liveWhen vanished the same way. Measured after on a 400px plate: one notch moves 0.50% against the old 2.00%, four times finer, and the ruler went 350px to 1400px. The max is deliberately unchanged per the entry's own warning, which also keeps saved projects safe — every value the old 0.02 step could hold is an exact multiple of 0.005, asserted over all 51 old positions, so nothing re-renders. The readout shows three decimals now; at two, half the values the slider can hold would have displayed as the same number. Verified at 380px: the row fits at 332px, the 1400px ruler sits inside an overflow-hidden strip, and the page does not scroll sideways. 966 tests green.

Most of “behaves like an effect” was already true and checking that first is what kept this small: #360 had already given masks the chevron, grip, eye, bin, swipe-to-delete and hold-to-reorder through the same attachFxGestures an effect uses, and “+ Add mask” is long gone because Mask is an entry in the effect browser, so the add route was shared already. What was left is what he can see — the separate block and heading are gone, the rows are appended to the same .fx-list, and they carry fx-row/fx-head so the card matches on all five measured properties (it had used --line where an effect uses --line-soft, and its own padding against .fx-row's zero). The head order is aligned too: the mask put its EYE before the chevron, so the disclosure arrow started in a different column from every other row. The missing swipe wrapper was not cosmetic: `.fx-row > .fx-swipe-wrap > .fx-head > .fx-disc` is how the open-chevron rule is scoped, so a mask's arrow never rotated when opened — the one thing a disclosure triangle must not do — and attachFxGestures slides row._wrap to reveal the delete panel, so with no wrapper the whole card slid with nothing behind it. Measured after: one list, chevrons aligned to the pixel, identical card styling, the row still opens with Mode/Feather/Opacity/Invert and the eye still toggles. The MODEL is deliberately unchanged and the test asserts that rather than implying a migration: masks are still layer.masks and the compositor still applies them at a different stage, which shows up in exactly one place — a mask cannot be dragged past an effect, only among masks. Lifting that is the 30-call-site job #360 sized, and it is his call. 967 tests green.
- v12.77 — **zooming no longer breaks the edit points, and the same fault is fixed in the mask editor (queue 561).** The entry's guess was exactly right for once: it is queue 165.3 again, in a different file. Every on-canvas overlay is a CHILD of #canvas-wrap, the element the viewport transform scales, so its CSS box is in the WRAPPER's coordinates while getBoundingClientRect() answers in SCREEN coordinates — writing one into the other applies the zoom twice. Measured on #pe-overlay against the preview canvas: 1x ratio 1.00 offset 0,0; 2x overlay 996x892 against a 498x446 canvas, ratio 2.00, offset 0,89; 4x overlay 2065x1784, ratio 4.00, offset 720,1200 — four times too big and 720x1200 out of place, so the handles land nowhere near the shape. He was right about “and probably other stuff”: the sweep found the MASK editor broken identically. Also swept — the selection box is fine (its ratio to the canvas holds and --vz keeps its handles 10px on screen), and the drawing overlay was already fixed at v8.00. A first check of mine wrongly said the selection box drifted; that was the instrument, because the canvas is CLIPPED at high zoom rather than scaled, and comparing against the shape's actual rendered pixels showed 0,0,1,1 agreement. crop-tool carried the identical line and is fixed by the same change, verified by source rather than a live session because it will not open on a shape layer. THE STRUCTURAL PART: this was the third time that rule had been written out by hand, so it is now one function — FM.placeOverlayOnCanvas in js/canvas-edit.js — and the test refuses a fourth copy, failing if any overlay module stops calling it or writes a raw screen rect into its box again. One wrong attempt worth recording: sizing the overlay from offsetWidth positions it correctly and then rasterises the backing store in wrapper space, so at 4x the handles would be drawn small and stretched up — right place, soft picture. The v8.00 fix divides the SCREEN rect by the wrapper's own render ratio, keeping the box right and the backing store at screen resolution. After: ratio 0.999-1.000 and offset 0,0 at 0.5x, 1x, 2x and 4x, backing store growing 499 -> 996 -> 1032 so the handles stay sharp. 968 tests green.
- v12.78 — **the ▶ preview on sound effects makes a sound (queue 562), and it was 100% broken rather than flaky — all 29 recipes threw.** The entry's suspicion was wrong and measuring showed it: it guessed a suspended AudioContext with no user gesture, and the context measured `running`. The real cause was that preview() built `Object.create(liveCtx)` and redefined `destination` on it so the recipes would connect to a trim gain instead of the speakers. A plain object with the context as its PROTOTYPE has none of the context's internal slots and native methods check for those, so through it createOscillator(), createBuffer(), currentTime and sampleRate all throw TypeError: Illegal invocation — only `destination` worked, being the one own property redefined. Every recipe threw on its first line, and the whole body sat inside `catch (e) {}` so nothing was ever reported: silent, no error, indistinguishable from a muted phone. THE PROXY WAS NEVER NEEDED — renderBuffer, the ADD path that works, already calls def.render(ctx, 0, dur, trim); the destination is the FOURTH ARGUMENT and 36 recipe bodies end in connect(out). Preview simply was not passing it, and the fix is that one argument. Measured both ways by rendering every recipe offline: old shape 29 of 29 threw Illegal invocation, new shape 29 of 29 audible with peaks 0.096 to 0.941 and none silent. resume() is awaited now as well — it returns a promise and the old code scheduled against currentTime straight after calling it, so a suspended context could schedule into the past; that was NOT the cause and is fixed because it is wrong. Failures are reported instead of swallowed, which is the second half of the fix: the silence is the only reason this lasted. The test pins the trap as well as the fix, asserting the prototype-proxy still throws, so if an engine ever makes it work the explanation gets revisited rather than quietly rotting. 969 tests green.
- v12.79 — **a Bell in the generated sound-effect library (queue 563), built so it is not the Ding twice.** The risk here was duplication rather than silence: `ding` sits directly above it and its own comment already claims to be “a bell rather than a beep” — two sine partials a fifth apart — so a third sine would have been the same sound under a second name, and no “does it make a noise” assertion would have noticed. It is built the way a struck bell behaves instead: inharmonic hum/prime/tierce/quint/nominal partials, with the tierce a MINOR third at 1.2x because that interval is what makes a bell sound like a bell; the high partials decaying first (1.00 down to 0.16 as the ratio rises) so the tone darkens as it rings rather than fading evenly like a synth; an 18ms band-passed noise strike for the clapper, without which the note fades in like a pad however fast the envelope is; and a 7-cent detune on the prime so the closest partials beat. Measured against the Ding rather than asserted — still ringing at 1.0s at 0.0112 against the Ding's 0.0010, brightness 0.088 falling to 0.066, and a strike of 0.432 rms in the first 20ms against 0.151 at 200ms. The first version CLIPPED, which is easy to miss and worth recording: renderBuffer normalises so an ADDED clip is always safe whatever a recipe does, but preview() plays the raw render through a fixed 0.82 gain, so a loud recipe clips on the ▶ and nowhere else — measured at 1.244 raw = 1.02 in preview, rescaled to 1.059 raw = 0.869. The test asserts that specifically. Measuring every recipe for this also found Reverse swell (1.121) and Glass break (1.011) already clipping in preview; logged as #566 rather than quietly changed, because it alters how two of his existing sounds play. 970 tests green.

Measured at 380px, those 34px boxes have a border width of ZERO, so nothing on the row is 34px to the eye; what you see is each button's 21x21 glyph. The pill is 84x21 now, centred to 0px against the glyph centres, digits unclipped — and the entry had offered exactly this overrule at v12.56 (“say icons and it is a one-number change”). 567 is him revoking half of queue 550: having lived with the dashes stopping at the head divider he asked for them back over it, keeping the right-hand stop at the project end — one number, --ar-x0 from the head width to 0, measured after at 0px start, 315.6 against a 316 project end, + unmoved. Clause 1 of 550 is marked REVOKED rather than un-ticked because it was built and delivered, and the test that pinned it was rewritten to guard the opposite direction so a later session cannot restore it from reading the entry alone. 565 gives a scrolling filter row page dots — his own suggestion, in the add menu's vocabulary (.addmenu-dot, spans not buttons, for the reason js/addmenu.js records) — with nothing drawn at all for rows that fit; measured, the 8-tile row shows 2 dots and the six that fit show none at 0px height, and the active dot tracks the scroll. The entry offered two routes: scale the two offenders (cheap, and the next loud recipe brings it straight back) or normalise the preview itself (structural, but it would make the ▶ do a full offline pass before every preview purely to learn its peak — real latency on a control that should feel instant). Worth restating because it is what makes the change safe: scaling a recipe does not alter how it sounds once ADDED, since renderBuffer normalises to its own target relative to the recipe's own peak — preview is the one path where absolute level matters, because it is the one path that is not normalised. 972 tests green.

- v12.89 — **text animations went from five to eleven (queue 573).** He was right that it was thin: the five that existed — Fade in, Fade up, Typewriter, Pop, Slide in — are all ONE idea when measured against each other, an ENTRANCE built from alpha, a shift and a scale. So the six new ones each differ from their nearest existing relative in KIND, not degree: Drop in bounces from the opposite direction to Fade up, Spin in ROTATES (nothing could until now), Zoom in from big falls in from oversized where Pop grows from nothing, Stretch is the first non-uniform scale, and Wave and Jitter are a new CATEGORY that never settles. Measured at 1080x1080: every preset differs from None (2,129-25,814px), each new one differs from its closest old relative (5,548-22,009px — the queue-563 Bell/Ding check), wave and jitter still move at t=2.0-2.25 (5,175 and 7,417) where fade and pop are exactly 0, and jitter renders the same frame identically twice because it hashes rather than using Math.random — random would boil rather than shake and the export would not match the preview.
- v12.90 — **stacked captions both show (queue 574).** One line caused it: `FM.activeCaption` kept exactly ONE cue via `(!hit || c.start > hit.start)` and silently discarded the rest, so the drop happened before the renderer ever saw it — the editor let him stack two and one simply never appeared, with no error. Every cue live at that instant is now returned joined by a newline, which is what "one on top of the other" means to the text renderer: it already splits on newlines, so stacked captions inherit alignment, line height and animation rather than needing a second layout path. Measured at 1080x1080 and the ink sums exactly — 7,848 alone, 12,412 alone, 20,260 overlapping. Order is start then ORIGINAL INDEX so same-instant cues cannot silently swap and the export keeps matching the preview; empty cues are skipped so they cannot add a blank line; and the single-caption case is byte-identical, asserted as the control.

Each row now carries a ↔ grip, about a second per 50px, with the typed fields kept for precision and updating live. The first build did nothing for a reason worth keeping: with the listener on the grip, a dispatched drag fired pointermove and pointerup and NEVER fired pointerdown — something above this panel swallows it in the CAPTURE phase, so any drag control added in here is dead on arrival and fails looking exactly like the bug it was meant to fix. It may overlap the next cue and leaves it intact, which is only safe because queue 574 shipped last tick; it stops at the layer end, cannot collapse, and is one undo step per drag.

Verified all three directions at 380px: a still 340ms hold arms, a 20px scroll during the hold does not, and a 100ms tap does not. 550 was chosen to match the Add menu long-press and the Presets card hold, which was right for a gesture nobody had complained about; he has now complained, so the feel he is actually holding wins — those two are deliberately untouched. - v12.94 — **Motion Blur (Footage) no longer defaults to the pixelated mode (#578 clause 1 — the entry STAYS OPEN for clause 2).** `def: 0` → `def: 1` (Smear) with `legacy: 0`. Pixel Motion is an optical-flow ESTIMATE and where the estimate is poor it tears the picture into blocks, which is the "pixelated" he means; Smear degrades to a soft streak instead, while Echo and Blend are stylistic rather than general-purpose defaults. The real work was the entry warning: `def` applies to NEW instances, `legacy` is what an ABSENT key reads as, and every motionflow he has already placed was saved with no style key — without legacy:0 all of them would silently re-render as Smear on next open. The renderer agrees independently via `fparam(p, "style", 0, t)`. Clause 2 deliberately not started: "needs a lot of work" is not a spec and there is no real footage to judge against, so changing sliders by feel would be exactly the guessing the entry forbids.

Measuring it as a failed black-and-white filter was reading its NAME rather than its definition. The mono filters were correct all along: on a #c05030 frame with baseline colour spread 144, Silver 0, Noir 0, Newsprint 2.98. So the real work was clause 3 — Platinum (bright, airy), Ink (near-graphic, blacks crushed) and Fog (flat mid-grey haze). - v12.96 — **a "Crop to canvas" button beside Free crop (queue 580).** The entry guessed right that this is arithmetic rather than a mechanism: it writes the SAME `layer.crop` source-pixel rect the free tool writes, so Reset, the scrubbers and the crop overlay all keep working with no second code path. "Canvas size" is the project SHAPE and not its pixel count, which is the whole design — a 1080x1920 project and a 1920x1080 clip share no dimension, so copying width and height literally would be meaningless. What it does is take the largest rect with the project aspect that fits inside the source, centred. Verified on four shapes: landscape-in-portrait, portrait-in-landscape, square, and an already-matching clip — right aspect, inside the source, centred, and one dimension taken whole. That last check matters and is not obvious: neither dimension whole means picture thrown away for nothing, either exceeding the source means asking for pixels that do not exist, and both are silent on screen. Exposed as FM.cropToCanvasRect so the test drives the real function rather than a copy of the formula.
- v12.97 — **saving a FILTER as a preset no longer stores an empty shell (#581 blocker — the entry STAYS OPEN).** `capture` walked the registry params only, which is right for an ordinary effect and silently wrong for a container: a filter IS its children. Measured, capturing a Noir box returned `hasEffects: false` and threw nothing — the worst failure shape there is, because the preset saves, loads, faves and lists with the right name and the picture is simply gone, found much later with no error to connect it to. Now capture keeps the children, sanePreset carries them through the SAME validator a project load uses rather than trusting them because they arrived inside something checked, and makeInstance puts them back before that sanitiser runs so parent and children are validated by one pass. A trap worth keeping: do NOT guard the restore on FM.isFxContainer(inst) — it asks whether an instance HAS an effects array and a FRESH registry instance has no effects key, so the guard is false for every container (measured: captured 4, restored 0). Control asserts an ordinary effect keeps its params and gains no children.

- v13.06 — **the effects browser warns on the motion family too (#598 — found, not reported).** Measured: on a still shape both Motion Blur (Object) and Motion Blur (Footage) change 0 pixels and the browser said nothing. 572-s check could not catch it — fxDeadOnLayer proves an effect dead by pushing one PIXEL through the filter string, so it only reasons about COLOUR, and these two are dead because nothing MOVES. The app already knew: objectblur-s own description ends "It does nothing on a layer that is not moving", sitting in a paragraph he reads AFTER picking. Claimed only when provable — shape or text, no animated transform, no other effects, no behaviours — because a video moves by itself and an effect can move a layer without touching its transform. The control found a real bug in my own code: the memo key was layer + effect-count + id, and animating a layer changes the ANSWER while changing neither, so a cached "it never moves" would have survived him keyframing it. Key now carries the motion state.
